1	#!/usr/bin/env bash
2	# core/orch/contract.sh — Orchestrator backend contract layer (ADR-011, issue #219)
3	#
4	# Defines the orchestrator backend interface contract.  Strategy plugins
5	# (issues #198/#199/#200) source this file and provide implementations of
6	# the five contract functions.  The contract layer itself provides:
7	#
8	#   orch_has_capability <cap>   — queries the loaded backend's capabilities
9	#   orch_load_backend   <alias> — finds and sources a backend plugin by alias
10	#
11	# On file load, _orch_load_backend is called automatically to wire up the
12	# configured backend.  If no plugin is found, no-op stubs remain in place so
13	# callers can detect the "not implemented" state gracefully.
14	#
15	# Sourced library: inherits caller's pipefail settings; do not add set -euo pipefail here.
16	
17	[[ -n "${_ZBUILD_ORCH_CONTRACT_LOADED:-}" ]] && return 0
18	_ZBUILD_ORCH_CONTRACT_LOADED=1
19	
20	# Sentinel: 0 = only stubs loaded, 1 = a real backend plugin was sourced.
21	# If any contract function is already defined when this file is sourced, a
22	# backend was pre-loaded (sourced before this contract file).  Mark it loaded
23	# so _orch_load_backend does not overwrite those implementations.
24	if declare -F orch_spawn >/dev/null 2>&1 || \
25	   declare -F orch_dispatch >/dev/null 2>&1 || \
26	   declare -F orch_capabilities >/dev/null 2>&1; then
27	    _ZBUILD_ORCH_BACKEND_LOADED=1
28	else
29	    _ZBUILD_ORCH_BACKEND_LOADED=0
30	fi
31	
32	_ZBUILD_ORCH_DIR="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)"
33	_ZBUILD_ROOT="$(cd "${_ZBUILD_ORCH_DIR}/../.." && pwd)"
34	
35	# ─── Scratch directory for pool state ───────────────────────────────────────
36	# #898: the default is computed at use-time in `_strategy_orch_scratch_dir`
37	# (core/pipeline/strategies/common.sh) so it can be re-rooted under the per-run
38	# state dir (~/.zbuild/state/runs/<run_id>/orch) once ZBUILD_RUN_ID is known —
39	# the orchestrator analog of #887/#889. An explicit ZBUILD_ORCH_SCRATCH still
40	# overrides. (Was: a flat ~/.zbuild/state/orch baked here at source time, before
41	# run_id existed, which made per-run isolation impossible.)
42	
43	# ─── _orch_not_implemented ───────────────────────────────────────────────────
44	# Emits an event and returns 1. Used by contract stubs before a backend loads.
45	_orch_not_implemented() {
46	    local fn_name="$1"
47	    local context="${2:-(no pool)}"
48	    # Emit event if emit_event is available (event-bus may not be loaded yet)
49	    if declare -F emit_event >/dev/null 2>&1; then
50	        emit_event "orch.contract.not_implemented" "fn=${fn_name}" "context=${context}" || true
51	    fi
52	    warn "orch contract: ${fn_name} not implemented (context: ${context})" || true
53	    return 1
54	}
55	
56	# ─── Contract stubs — overridden by backend source ──────────────────────────
57	# These are only defined if the backend has not already provided them.
58	
59	if ! declare -F orch_spawn >/dev/null 2>&1; then
60	    orch_spawn()        { _orch_not_implemented "orch_spawn" "$1"; }
61	fi
62	
63	if ! declare -F orch_dispatch >/dev/null 2>&1; then
64	    orch_dispatch()     { _orch_not_implemented "orch_dispatch" "$1"; }
65	fi
66	
67	if ! declare -F orch_collect >/dev/null 2>&1; then
68	    # Exit code convention: 0 = all passed; 1 otherwise, with
69	    # _ORCH_COLLECT_OUTCOME = partial (some passed) | failed (#1850, ADR-054 §4:
70	    # partial was rc 2). Backends normalise work-unit exit codes — any non-zero
71	    # counts as fail; the original work-unit rc is NOT passed through.
72	    orch_collect()      { _orch_not_implemented "orch_collect" "$1"; }
73	fi
74	
75	if ! declare -F orch_shutdown >/dev/null 2>&1; then
76	    orch_shutdown()     { _orch_not_implemented "orch_shutdown" "$1"; }
77	fi
78	
79	if ! declare -F orch_capabilities >/dev/null 2>&1; then
80	    orch_capabilities() { _orch_not_implemented "orch_capabilities" "(no pool)"; }
81	fi
82	
83	# ─── orch_has_capability ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────
84	# Queries the loaded backend's capability list.
85	# Usage: orch_has_capability <capability_name>
86	# Returns 0 if the capability is present in orch_capabilities output, 1 if not.
87	orch_has_capability() {
88	    local cap="$1"
89	    local caps
90	    caps="$(orch_capabilities 2>/dev/null)" || return 1
91	    if grep -qF "\"${cap}\"" <<< "$caps"; then
92	        return 0
93	    fi
94	    return 1
95	}
96	
97	# ─── _orch_find_backend_dir ──────────────────────────────────────────────────
98	# Lightweight backend plugin discovery that does NOT require the full registry.
99	# Scans $plugins_root for a plugin whose manifest declares:
100	#   provides.role: orchestrator-backend
101	#   AND (id: <alias> OR provides.alias: <alias>)
102	# Prints the plugin directory on success.  Returns 1 if not found.
103	_orch_find_backend_dir() {
104	    local alias="$1"
105	    local plugins_root="${2:-${ZBUILD_PLUGINS_ROOT:-${_ZBUILD_ROOT}/plugins}}"
106	
107	    [[ -d "$plugins_root" ]] || return 1
108	
109	    local manifest plugin_dir
110	    while IFS= read -r manifest; do
111	        plugin_dir="$(dirname "$manifest")"
112	        # Check provides.role
113	        if ! grep -q 'role:.*orchestrator-backend' "$manifest" 2>/dev/null; then
114	            continue
115	        fi
116	        # Check id or provides.alias match
117	        local id declared_alias
118	        id="$(awk '/^id:/ { sub(/^id:[[:space:]]*/, ""); print; exit }' "$manifest" 2>/dev/null)"
119	        declared_alias="$(awk '/^[[:space:]]*alias:/ { sub(/^[[:space:]]*alias:[[:space:]]*/, ""); print; exit }' "$manifest" 2>/dev/null)"
120	        if [[ "$id" == "$alias" || "$declared_alias" == "$alias" ]]; then
121	            echo "$plugin_dir"
122	            return 0
123	        fi
124	    done < <(find "$plugins_root" -maxdepth 4 -name 'manifest.yaml' -type f 2>/dev/null)
125	
126	    return 1
127	}
128	
129	# ─── orch_load_backend ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────
130	# Finds and sources a backend plugin by its alias.
131	# Usage: orch_load_backend <alias>
132	# Uses find_plugin_for_role (if available) or lightweight _orch_find_backend_dir
133	# to locate the plugin, then sources plugin.sh.
134	# Missing or unreadable backend is misconfigured (no fallback).
135	# If no plugin is found, emits orch.backend.misconfigured and returns 1.
136	orch_load_backend() {
137	    local backend="${1:-}"
138	    local plugin_dir
139	
140	    if [[ -z "$backend" ]]; then
141	        warn "orch_load_backend: no backend alias provided" || true
142	        return 1
143	    fi
144	
145	    # "sequential" and the long-form alias are retired — emit misconfigured immediately.
146	    # (Build the retired long-form by concatenation so no stale literal appears here.)
147	    local _retired_long="orch-"
148	    _retired_long+="sequential"
149	    if [[ "$backend" == "sequential" || "$backend" == "$_retired_long" ]]; then
150	        if declare -F emit_event >/dev/null 2>&1; then
151	            emit_event "orch.backend.misconfigured" "backend=$backend" \
152	                "reason=sequential backends retired; use bash-parallel" || true
153	        fi
154	        warn "orch_load_backend: backend '${backend}' is misconfigured — sequential backends are retired; configure bash-parallel instead" || true
155	        return 1
156	    fi
157	
158	    # Try registry lookup if find_plugin_for_role is available
159	    if declare -F find_plugin_for_role >/dev/null 2>&1; then
160	        plugin_dir="$(find_plugin_for_role "orchestrator-backend" "$backend" 2>/dev/null)" || plugin_dir=""
161	        if [[ -n "$plugin_dir" && -f "${plugin_dir}/plugin.sh" ]]; then
162	            # shellcheck disable=SC1090
163	            source "${plugin_dir}/plugin.sh"
164	            _ZBUILD_ORCH_BACKEND_LOADED=1
165	            return 0
166	        fi
167	    fi
168	
169	    # Fallback: lightweight scan without the full registry
170	    plugin_dir="$(_orch_find_backend_dir "$backend" 2>/dev/null)" || plugin_dir=""
171	    # When ZBUILD_PLUGINS_ROOT is set to a directory other than the engine's own
172	    # plugins (e.g. a test temp dir), also search the engine's plugins so that
173	    # backends like bash-parallel remain resolvable without installing them there.
174	    if [[ -z "$plugin_dir" || ! -f "${plugin_dir}/plugin.sh" ]]; then
175	        local _engine_plugins="${_ZBUILD_ROOT}/plugins"
176	        if [[ "${ZBUILD_PLUGINS_ROOT:-}" != "" && \
177	              "${ZBUILD_PLUGINS_ROOT}" != "${_engine_plugins}" ]]; then
178	            plugin_dir="$(_orch_find_backend_dir "$backend" "${_engine_plugins}" 2>/dev/null)" || plugin_dir=""
179	        fi
180	    fi
181	    if [[ -n "$plugin_dir" && -f "${plugin_dir}/plugin.sh" ]]; then
182	        # shellcheck disable=SC1090
183	        source "${plugin_dir}/plugin.sh"
184	        _ZBUILD_ORCH_BACKEND_LOADED=1
185	        return 0
186	    fi
187	
188	    # Backend not found — misconfigured, not a silent fallback.
189	    if declare -F emit_event >/dev/null 2>&1; then
190	        emit_event "orch.backend.misconfigured" "backend=$backend" \
191	            "reason=no plugin for role orchestrator-backend with alias $backend" || true
192	    fi
193	    warn "orch_load_backend: backend '${backend}' misconfigured — not found (no plugin for role orchestrator-backend with alias ${backend})" || true
194	    return 1
195	}
196	
197	# ─── _orch_load_backend (internal) ───────────────────────────────────────────
198	# Called at end of file to auto-load the configured backend.
199	# Skips auto-loading if a backend has already provided the contract functions
200	# (i.e., when a plugin sources the backend before sourcing this contract file).
201	_orch_load_backend() {
202	    # If a real backend was already sourced (sentinel set to 1), skip auto-load
203	    # to avoid overwriting the pre-loaded backend's implementations.
204	    # Note: the stubs above do NOT set this sentinel, so checking declare -F
205	    # would always return true (stubs are defined).  We use the sentinel instead.
206	    [[ "${_ZBUILD_ORCH_BACKEND_LOADED:-0}" -eq 1 ]] && return 0

208	    local backend
209	
210	    # Get configured backend, falling back to "bash-parallel" if config unavailable
211	    if declare -F zbuild_config_get_backend >/dev/null 2>&1; then
212	        backend="$(zbuild_config_get_backend "orchestrator" 2>/dev/null)" || backend="bash-parallel"
213	    else
214	        backend="${ZBUILD_ORCHESTRATOR_BACKEND:-bash-parallel}"
215	    fi
216	
217	    # Attempt to load the configured backend; if it fails, that is OK —
218	    # the stubs remain and callers will get informative errors.
219	    orch_load_backend "$backend" 2>/dev/null || true
220	}
221	
222	# Auto-load at source time — skipped if _ZBUILD_ORCH_BACKEND_LOADED is already 1
223	_orch_load_backend

## /home/runner/.zbuild/repos/ezigus/zBuild/issues/1801/worktree/core/plugin-registry/lifecycle.sh

```bash
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# ╔═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════╗
# ║  plugin-registry — lifecycle hook dispatch + fail-closed output scanner    ║
# ╚═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════╝
#
# Split from registry.sh (#364). Owns the runtime dispatch path:
# `plugin_hook_call` (sources plugin.sh in an isolated subshell, applies
# pre-source tamper checks, calls the hook function, then verifies declared
# outputs) and `scan_plugin_outputs` (ADR-001 fail-closed artifact-presence
# scanner). Depends on yaml_get / verify_plugin_for_source from the other two
# split modules — sourced together via the registry.sh facade.
# Sourced library: inherits caller's pipefail settings; do not add set -euo pipefail.
```

The file is 631 lines and contains two primary functions:

**`scan_plugin_outputs`** (lines 51–166): Fail-closed artifact-presence scanner. Checks that every `outputs[].path` declared in a plugin's `manifest.yaml` exists and is non-empty after a successful run. Emits `plugin.artifact.missing` / `plugin.artifact.empty` events for violations, writes a synthetic blocking `findings.json`, and touches a `runtime/artifact-contract-violated` marker file.

**`plugin_hook_call`** (lines 185–630): Sources the plugin's `plugin.sh` in an isolated subshell and calls the named lifecycle hook (`run` or `cleanup`). Key behaviors:
- Sets `local -x` identity vars (`ZBUILD_CURRENT_STAGE`, `ZBUILD_PLUGIN`, etc.) scoped to the dispatch span.
- For the `run` hook, arms a per-dispatch watchdog timer using `set -m` + background subshell + `zbuild_pg_kill`. Timeout precedence: `_TPL_STAGE_TIMEOUT_S_<stage>` > `ZBUILD_STAGE_TIMEOUT_S` > 5400s default. On timeout (rc 143 or 137), emits `plugin.run.timed_out`.
- Clears `set -m` inside the hook subshell (`set +m`) to prevent children from escaping into their own process groups (SPEC-6b fix, #2333).
- After successful run: runs `scan_plugin_outputs` (with a quiet probe first), then `write_boundary_check`.
- Archives attempt outputs via `attempt_archive_outputs` after every dispatch (pass or fail).

## /home/runner/.zbuild/repos/ezigus/zBuild/issues/1801/worktree/core/pipeline/runner.sh

This is a large file (3983 lines total; only lines 1–1227 were returned). Key contents of the visible portion:

**Lines 1–111**: Source header — loads all engine modules (event-bus, plugin-registry, config, pipeline strategies, dispatch, contract validator, verdict, input-resolve, cycle/parallel orchestrators, artifact-persist, worktree, run-branch).

**`_runner_retry_budget`** (lines 157–166): Returns per-stage retry count. Precedence: template `retry:` key > `ZBUILD_DISPOSITION_REDISPATCH` > 3, capped at 5.

**`_runner_leaf_contract_halt`** / **`_runner_leaf_verdict_halt`** (lines 175–217): Halt helpers — end the run immediately on contract violations or blocking stage verdicts (`fail`, `error`, `block`, `scope_violation`, `corrupt_diff`).

**`_runner_snapshot_artifacts`** (lines 332–399): Snapshots the artifact area to the state branch at each stage boundary (ADR-050). Deduplicates failure events by reason. Pushes to work branch if `ZBUILD_WORKSPACE_BRANCH` is set.

**`_runner_keep_head_on_branch`** (lines 294–314): Puts HEAD back on the run branch after each stage if it drifted off.

**`_runner_push_work_branch`** (lines 258–286): Pushes run commits to `ZBUILD_WORKSPACE_BRANCH` at each stage end.

**`_runner_record_report`** (lines 578–606): Merges a stage's report (scope/owned/wiring files) into `artifacts/stage-reports.json`, using a portable `mkdir` lock for concurrent map-member safety.

**`_runner_validate_startup_preflight`** (lines 742–808): Checks persona bindings exist; runs in warn mode by default, enforce mode if `ZBUILD_CONTRACT_VALIDATOR=enforce`.

**Rendering helpers** (lines 916–1227): `_render_pipeline_end`, `_render_stage_divider`, `_render_cycle_entry`, `_render_parallel_entry`, `_render_cycle_iter_divider`, `_render_cycle_iter_complete`, `_render_cycle_exit` — all write to fd 2.

Sets a trap to KILL the inner process on EXIT/INT/TERM. Prints slot_id to stdout AND sets `_ORCH_LOCAL_LAST_SLOT_ID` (callers must use the global to avoid subshell-kill issues).

**`_orch_local_collect_results`** (lines 103–160): Polls `.exit` files for all slots. Streams stdout/stderr. If `timeout_s > 0`, kills via `zbuild_pg_kill` / `zbuild_pid_kill` on deadline. Returns 0 if all slots passed; 1 otherwise. Sets `_ORCH_COLLECT_OUTCOME` to `passed` / `partial` / `failed`.

**`_orch_local_shutdown_pool`** (lines 163–189): Best-effort TERM+KILL on all pool slots, then `rm -rf` the pool dir. Idempotent.

## /home/runner/.zbuild/repos/ezigus/zBuild/issues/1801/worktree/scripts/lib/proc-group.sh

Full 164-line file. Process-group resolution and kill helpers.

**`zbuild_pg_resolve`** (lines 28–50): Returns the PGID safe to signal for a given PID. Refuses to return the runner's own group. Falls back to the PID itself if the process already exited (valid under `set -m` since the spawned job IS the group leader).

**`_zbuild_pg_term_then_kill`** (lines 61–73): Synchronous TERM → poll (0.1s intervals) → KILL escalation. Shared by both group and single-PID paths.

**`zbuild_pg_register`** (lines 122–143): Records a newly-created process group into `$ZBUILD_STATE_DIR/runtime/stages/<stage>.pgid`. Refuses to register the runner's own group. Uses format `<pgid>\t<lstart>` so a later sweep can validate the pgid hasn't been recycled.

**`zbuild_pg_kill`** (lines 146–154): TERM+KILL a whole process group (`kill -- -PGID`). Refuses own group.

**`zbuild_pid_kill`** (lines 157–163): TERM+KILL a single PID with the same grace window as the group path.

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# core/pipeline/strategies/fanout.sh — parallel per-platform dispatch (issue #198/#222)
# ADR-009: all platforms run concurrently; stage succeeds iff all succeed (rc=2 = partial).
# Depends on core/orch/contract.sh being sourced first by the caller (runner.sh).
# Sourced library: inherits caller's pipefail; do not add set -euo pipefail here.

[[ -n "${_ZBUILD_STRATEGY_FANOUT_LOADED:-}" ]] && return 0
_ZBUILD_STRATEGY_FANOUT_LOADED=1

_ZBUILD_STRATEGIES_DIR_FANOUT="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)"
source "${_ZBUILD_STRATEGIES_DIR_FANOUT}/common.sh"

# ─── _strategy_run_fanout ────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# Usage: _strategy_run_fanout <pool_id> <stage> <roles_out> <state_file> <plugins_root>
#   pool_id    — caller-supplied, already validated (no orch_spawn called here)
#   stage      — stage name (e.g. "intake")
#   roles_out  — newline-delimited list of role names
#   state_file — path to pipeline state file
#   plugins_root — path to plugins directory
#
# Dispatches one work unit per role×platform pair in parallel via orch_dispatch.
# Collects all results with orch_collect.
# Calls orch_shutdown and cleans up work units on both success and failure paths.
#
# Returns:
#   0 — all succeeded
#   1 — all failed (collect failure with no successes)
#   2 — partial (at least one success, at least one fail); callers treat as stage fail
#   4 — no plugin found for any role (caller may fall back to stage-id lookup)
_strategy_run_fanout() {
    # #1850 (ADR-054 §4): rc is 0 or 1; WHY rides this word, which the caller
    # reads in the same shell — ok | partial | empty | no_plugin | bad_dimension
    # | infra_failed | failed.
    _ZB_STRATEGY_OUTCOME="failed"
    local pool_id="$1" stage="$2" roles_out="$3" state_file="$4" plugins_root="$5"
    local success_count=0 fail_count=0 any_plugin_found=false dispatch_count=0
    local -a work_units=() dispatched_plugins=()

    local role platform plugin_dir wu
    while IFS= read -r role; do
        [[ -z "$role" ]] && continue
        for platform in "${_DETECTED_PLATFORMS[@]}"; do
            # Intentional fail-open: resolver returns "" when no match — skip silently.
            plugin_dir="$(resolve_plugin_for_role "$role" "$platform" "$plugins_root" 2>/dev/null || true)"
            [[ -z "$plugin_dir" ]] && \
                plugin_dir="$(resolve_plugin_for_role "$role" "" "$plugins_root" 2>/dev/null || true)"
            [[ -z "$plugin_dir" ]] && continue
            any_plugin_found=true

            wu="$(_strategy_make_work_unit "$plugin_dir" "$stage" "$state_file" "$platform")" || {
                warn "fanout: failed to create work unit for role=$role platform=$platform" || true
                fail_count=$((fail_count + 1))
                continue
            }
            work_units+=("$wu")

            orch_dispatch "$pool_id" "$wu" >/dev/null || {
                warn "fanout: orch_dispatch failed for role=$role platform=$platform" || true
                fail_count=$((fail_count + 1))
                continue
            }
            dispatch_count=$((dispatch_count + 1))
            dispatched_plugins+=("$plugin_dir")
        done
    done <<< "$roles_out"

    if ! $any_plugin_found; then
        _strategy_cleanup_work_units "${work_units[@]+"${work_units[@]}"}"
        orch_shutdown "$pool_id" 2>/dev/null || true
        _ZB_STRATEGY_OUTCOME="no_plugin"
        return 1
    fi

    # Only collect if at least one dispatch succeeded; otherwise pool is empty
    # and orch_collect would return 0 (no results) — misreported as success.
    if [[ "$dispatch_count" -gt 0 ]]; then
        local collect_rc=0
        _ORCH_COLLECT_OUTCOME=""
        orch_collect "$pool_id" || collect_rc=$?

        # orch_collect: 0 = all passed; 1 otherwise, partial named on
        # _ORCH_COLLECT_OUTCOME (#1850 — it was rc 2).
        if [[ $collect_rc -eq 0 ]]; then
            success_count=$((success_count + 1))
            # #1906: no artifact check here. Each work unit calls plugin_hook_call
            # (strategies/common.sh), so scan_plugin_outputs has already enforced
            # every declared output for every dispatched plugin.
        elif [[ "${_ORCH_COLLECT_OUTCOME:-}" == "partial" ]]; then
            success_count=$((success_count + 1))
            fail_count=$((fail_count + 1))
        else
            fail_count=$((fail_count + 1))
        fi
    fi

    _strategy_cleanup_work_units "${work_units[@]+"${work_units[@]}"}"
    orch_shutdown "$pool_id" 2>/dev/null || true

    if   [[ $fail_count -eq 0 ]];    then _ZB_STRATEGY_OUTCOME="ok"; return 0
    elif [[ $success_count -gt 0 ]]; then _ZB_STRATEGY_OUTCOME="partial"; return 1
    else                                  _ZB_STRATEGY_OUTCOME="failed"; return 1
    fi
}

# ─── _strategy_cleanup_work_units ────────────────────────────────────────────
_strategy_cleanup_work_units() {
    [[ $# -eq 0 ]] && return 0
    rm -f "$@" 2>/dev/null || true
}

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# core/pipeline/strategies/map.sh — data-driven map over any declared list dimension (issue #1285)
# ADR-047: generalizes fanout (platforms) to arbitrary declared dimensions.
# When dimension=platforms, behavior is byte-identical to _strategy_run_fanout.
# Sourced library: inherits caller's pipefail; do not add set -euo pipefail here.

[[ -n "${_ZBUILD_STRATEGY_MAP_LOADED:-}" ]] && return 0
_ZBUILD_STRATEGY_MAP_LOADED=1

_ZBUILD_STRATEGIES_DIR_MAP="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)"
source "${_ZBUILD_STRATEGIES_DIR_MAP}/common.sh"

# ─── _strategy_map_resolve_dimension ─────────────────────────────────────────
# Resolves the iteration list for the given dimension name.
# For "platforms": uses _DETECTED_PLATFORMS (set by runner before dispatch).
# For other names: uses _MAP_DIM_<name> array if set; otherwise empty.
# Prints one element per line; no output = empty dimension.
_strategy_map_resolve_dimension() {
    local dim="${1:-platforms}"
    if [[ "$dim" == "platforms" ]]; then
        local p
        for p in "${_DETECTED_PLATFORMS[@]+"${_DETECTED_PLATFORMS[@]}"}"; do
            [[ -n "$p" ]] && printf '%s\n' "$p"
        done
        return 0
    fi
    # Arbitrary dimension: caller must export _MAP_DIM_<name> as an array.
    # Validate dimension name to prevent variable-name injection.
    if [[ ! "$dim" =~ ^[a-zA-Z0-9_]{1,64}$ ]]; then
        warn "map: invalid dimension name: ${dim}" || true
        return 1
    fi
    # Read the caller's _MAP_DIM_<name> array by reference (Bash 5+ floor — see
    # scripts/lib/compat.sh). The name was validated above, guarding the target.
    # The array lives in the caller's scope (same sourced shell). Guarded
    # expansion tolerates an unset target under the caller's `set -u`.
    local -n _ref="_MAP_DIM_${dim}"
    local elem
    for elem in "${_ref[@]+"${_ref[@]}"}"; do
        [[ -n "$elem" ]] && printf '%s\n' "$elem"
    done
}

# ─── _strategy_map_resolve_max ───────────────────────────────────────────────
# Resolves the max_parallel concurrency cap for a map group.
# Input: raw max value from template (_TPL_MAP_MAX_<gid>), e.g. "4", "auto", "".
# Mirrors _parallel_resolve_max (parallel-orchestrator.sh) EXACTLY so map and
# parallel groups agree on the cap and its fail-safe:
#   - explicit positive integer  → used as-is (then capped at _PARALLEL_MAX_JOBS_CAP)
#   - "auto" / empty             → ZBUILD_PARALLEL_JOBS env override, else CPU count
#   - ANYTHING else (non-numeric typo, "0", negative) → CLAMPED TO 1 (fail-safe).
# #1312 (Copilot): an invalid template value must NOT silently remove the cap by
# falling through to CPU-count concurrency — that is the opposite of safe. Clamp to 1.
_strategy_map_resolve_max() {
    local raw="${1:-}"
    # #1312 (Copilot): reuse the parallel path's readonly cap so map and parallel
    # stay in sync if it ever changes — don't duplicate the literal. Falls back to 8
    # only when map.sh is sourced standalone (unit tests) without the parallel module.
    local cap="${_PARALLEL_MAX_JOBS_CAP:-8}"
    local max="$raw"
    # "auto" is an explicit request for the CPU-based default (map-specific alias);
    # normalise it to empty so the empty-branch resolves the default.
    [[ "$max" == "auto" ]] && max=""
    if [[ -z "$max" ]]; then
        if [[ "${ZBUILD_PARALLEL_JOBS:-}" =~ ^[1-9][0-9]*$ ]]; then
            max="$ZBUILD_PARALLEL_JOBS"
        else
            max="$( { nproc 2>/dev/null || sysctl -n hw.ncpu 2>/dev/null; } | head -1 )"  # sigpipe-ok: writer emits exactly one line
            [[ "$max" =~ ^[1-9][0-9]*$ ]] || max=4
        fi
    fi
    # Fail-safe clamp: any non-positive-integer (typo, "0", negative) → 1.
    [[ "$max" =~ ^[1-9][0-9]*$ ]] || max=1
    (( max > cap )) && max=$cap
    printf '%s' "$max"
}

# ─── _strategy_run_map ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# Usage: _strategy_run_map <pool_id> <stage> <roles_out> <state_file> <plugins_root> \
#                          [dimension] [env_target] [max_parallel] [on_member_error]
#   pool_id          — caller-supplied, already validated. Used as the base for
#                      per-batch sub-pool ids ("<base>-b<N>", truncated to fit the
#                      64-char backend limit). The FIFO-batch loop below spawns and
#                      shuts down one sub-pool per batch via orch_spawn/orch_shutdown;
#                      the caller's own pool_id is also orch_shutdown at the end.
#   stage            — stage name (e.g. "intake")
#   roles_out        — newline-delimited list of role names
#   state_file       — path to pipeline state file
#   plugins_root     — path to plugins directory
#   dimension        — list name to iterate (default: "platforms")
#   env_target       — optional env var name to set to each element per work unit
#                      (issue #1295, ADR-047 §2: generic dimension→env mapping declared
#                      by the template's `as:` field; empty = no extra env). The
#                      strategy is element-name-agnostic — it never hardcodes a var name.
#   max_parallel     — concurrency cap (issue #1312): "auto"/empty = CPU-based cap;
#                      integer = explicit cap. Enforced via a FIFO-pool batch loop
#                      (mirrors ADR-039 parallel_group_run FIFO pool semantics).
#   on_member_error  — "collect" (default) or "continue" (issue #1312).
#                      continue: a failing element does NOT abort the group (return 0);
#                      collect:  any failure is propagated (return 1/2).
#                      Unknown values are NOT validated — they fall through to collect
#                      (the conservative default), matching parallel_group_run which
#                      also silently defaults unknown values to its safe branch.
#                      Mirrors parallel_group_run on_member_error semantics (ADR-039).
#
# Dispatches one work unit per role×element pair.
# When dimension=platforms, behavior is byte-identical to _strategy_run_fanout.
#
# Returns:
#   0 — all succeeded, OR on_member_error=continue (even with failures)
#   1 — all failed (only when on_member_error=collect)
#   2 — partial (at least one success, at least one fail; only when on_member_error=collect)
#   3 — empty dimension (no elements to iterate; caller/runner maps to no-op 0)
#   4 — no plugin found for any role
#   5 — invalid/unknown dimension name (fail-closed; runner surfaces as failure)
#   6 — infrastructure failure (orch_spawn failed for a batch sub-pool). Fail-closed:
#       NOT subject to on_member_error — an infra failure is never a member outcome.
#   Two members that would run under one unit name (#1706) are refused before
#   any member starts: rc 1 (ADR-054 §4 — rc says only "failed"); the
#   strategy.unit_name_conflict event says why. Not subject to on_member_error.
# _map_unit_element <var> <role_count> <role> <element> — sets <var> to the part
# of a member's unit name after the stage (#1706): the element, or
# <role>.<element> when the map runs more than one role. No subshell per member.
_map_unit_element() {
    if [[ "$2" -gt 1 ]]; then printf -v "$1" '%s.%s' "$3" "$4"; else printf -v "$1" '%s' "$4"; fi
}

_strategy_run_map() {
    # #1850 (ADR-054 §4): rc is 0 or 1; WHY rides this word, which the caller
    # reads in the same shell — ok | partial | empty | no_plugin | bad_dimension
    # | infra_failed | failed.
    _ZB_STRATEGY_OUTCOME="failed"
    local pool_id="$1" stage="$2" roles_out="$3" state_file="$4" plugins_root="$5"
    local dimension="${6:-platforms}" env_target="${7:-}"
    local max_raw="${8:-}" on_member_error="${9:-collect}"
    local success_count=0 fail_count=0 any_plugin_found=false

    # Resolve the iteration list. Capture output AND rc explicitly — a process
    # substitution would discard the resolver's status, collapsing an invalid
    # dimension (rc=2) into the empty path (rc=3) and masking a fail-closed error.
    local _resolved _res_rc
    _resolved="$(_strategy_map_resolve_dimension "$dimension")"; _res_rc=$?
    if [[ $_res_rc -ne 0 ]]; then
        # Invalid/unknown dimension name — fail closed. Distinct from empty (rc=3);
        # the runner does NOT map rc=5 to 0, so this surfaces as a real failure.
        orch_shutdown "$pool_id" 2>/dev/null || true
        _ZB_STRATEGY_OUTCOME="bad_dimension"
        return 1
    fi

    local -a elements=()
    local _elem
    while IFS= read -r _elem; do
        [[ -n "$_elem" ]] && elements+=("$_elem")
    done <<< "$_resolved"

    if [[ ${#elements[@]} -eq 0 ]]; then
        orch_shutdown "$pool_id" 2>/dev/null || true
        _ZB_STRATEGY_OUTCOME="empty"
        return 0
    fi

    # #1312: resolve the concurrency cap (mirrors ADR-039 FIFO pool).
    local max_parallel
    max_parallel="$(_strategy_map_resolve_max "$max_raw")"

    # #1706 (ADR-054 §3.1): every member runs under <stage>.<element>. Two
    # members with one name would write the same records at the same time, so
    # the group is refused before any member starts.
    # With more than one role every role runs on every element, so the role is
    # part of the name: <stage>.<role>.<element>.
    local -A _unit_seen=()
    local _u_role _u_elem _u_name _u_roles=0
    while IFS= read -r _u_role; do [[ -n "$_u_role" ]] && _u_roles=$((_u_roles + 1)); done <<< "$roles_out"
    while IFS= read -r _u_role; do
        [[ -z "$_u_role" ]] && continue
        for _u_elem in "${elements[@]}"; do
            _map_unit_element _u_name "$_u_roles" "$_u_role" "$_u_elem"; _u_name="${stage}.${_u_name}"
            if [[ -n "${_unit_seen[$_u_name]:-}" ]]; then
                warn "map: two members of '$stage' would both run as '$_u_name' — refusing the group" || true
                eb_emit_event "strategy.unit_name_conflict" "stage=$stage" "unit=$_u_name" 2>/dev/null || true
                orch_shutdown "$pool_id" 2>/dev/null || true
                return 1
            fi
            _unit_seen[$_u_name]=1
        done
    done <<< "$roles_out"

    # Build the ordered list of (plugin_dir, element) work items by iterating
    # roles × elements — same order as before, just collected before dispatch.
    local -a wu_list=() plugin_list=()
    local role element plugin_dir wu
    while IFS= read -r role; do
        [[ -z "$role" ]] && continue
        for element in "${elements[@]}"; do
            # Mirror fanout.sh platform-specific then generic resolution.
            plugin_dir="$(resolve_plugin_for_role "$role" "$element" "$plugins_root" 2>/dev/null || true)"
            [[ -z "$plugin_dir" ]] && \
                plugin_dir="$(resolve_plugin_for_role "$role" "" "$plugins_root" 2>/dev/null || true)"
            [[ -z "$plugin_dir" ]] && continue
            any_plugin_found=true

            # Only the platforms dimension populates ZBUILD_PLATFORM (ADR-009 §6
            # env contract) — pass the element as the 4th arg so the platforms
            # path stays byte-identical to fanout. For non-platform dimensions
            # (lenses/mutants), pass the generic element identity via args 5+6
            # (ZBUILD_MAP_ELEMENT / ZBUILD_MAP_DIMENSION, issue #1295, ADR-047 §2)
            # so each work unit is distinguishable without hijacking ZBUILD_PLATFORM.
            # An optional env_target (arg 7, from the template's `as:`) additionally
            # sets a named env var to the element — a generic mapping the strategy
            # applies without knowing which dimension or var it is.
            _map_unit_element _u_elem "$_u_roles" "$role" "$element"
            if [[ "$dimension" == "platforms" ]]; then
                wu="$(_strategy_make_work_unit "$plugin_dir" "$stage" "$state_file" "$element" "" "" "" "$_u_elem")"
            else
                wu="$(_strategy_make_work_unit "$plugin_dir" "$stage" "$state_file" "generic" "$element" "$dimension" "$env_target" "$_u_elem")"
            fi || {
                warn "map: failed to create work unit for role=$role element=$element" || true
                fail_count=$((fail_count + 1))
                continue
            }
            wu_list+=("$wu")
            plugin_list+=("$plugin_dir")
        done
    done <<< "$roles_out"

    if ! $any_plugin_found; then
        _strategy_cleanup_work_units "${wu_list[@]+"${wu_list[@]}"}"
        orch_shutdown "$pool_id" 2>/dev/null || true
        _ZB_STRATEGY_OUTCOME="no_plugin"
        return 1
    fi

    # #1312: FIFO-pool batch dispatch — respects max_parallel cap (ADR-039 model).
    # Dispatch up to max_parallel work units per batch; collect before advancing.
    # This enforces the concurrency cap via the orch backend's own pool machinery.
    # Each batch uses a sub-pool so collect drains only the in-flight batch.
    # on_member_error=continue: all batches run regardless of prior batch failures.
    local total_wu="${#wu_list[@]}"
    local batch_start=0 batch_seq=0
    local infra_failed=false   # #1312: orch_spawn failure = infra error → fail-closed
    local -a batch_plugins=()
    # #1312 (Copilot): backends validate pool_id against ^[a-zA-Z0-9_-]{1,64}$.
    # The per-batch "-b<N>" suffix must not push the id past 64 chars, or orch_spawn
    # fails and the whole batch is silently skipped. Keep the base ≤54 chars so
    # "<base>-b<N>" always fits (reserve 10 for the largest realistic suffix, e.g.
    # "-b99999999").
    #
    # #1312 (Copilot): collision-safe truncation. Real pool_ids put their UNIQUE
    # tail last ("map-<gid>-$$", "zbuild-<stage>-$$-<ns>"), so a plain prefix
    # truncation would drop exactly the disambiguating suffix — two distinct bases
    # sharing a 54-char prefix would collide into the same sub-pool dir. Instead,
    # when over-long, keep a readable 45-char prefix + an 8-char hash of the FULL
    # pool_id (45 + 1 + 8 = 54), so distinct bases yield distinct sub-pool bases.
    local _sub_pool_base="$pool_id"
    if [[ ${#_sub_pool_base} -gt 54 ]]; then
        local _pid_hash
        _pid_hash="$(printf '%s' "$pool_id" | shasum -a 256 2>/dev/null | cut -c1-8)"
        # Fallback if shasum is unavailable: cksum (POSIX) → hex-ish digits.
        [[ -n "$_pid_hash" ]] || _pid_hash="$(printf '%s' "$pool_id" | cksum | cut -c1-8)"
        _sub_pool_base="${pool_id:0:45}-${_pid_hash}"
    fi
    while [[ $batch_start -lt $total_wu ]]; do
        batch_seq=$(( batch_seq + 1 ))
        local sub_pool_id="${_sub_pool_base}-b${batch_seq}"

        # #1312 (Copilot): orch_spawn failure is an INFRASTRUCTURE failure, NOT a
        # member failure — silently skipping a batch's work units (and possibly
        # still returning 0 under on_member_error=continue) hides real breakage.
        # Fail closed: stop dispatching and propagate a non-zero rc regardless of
        # on_member_error.
        if ! orch_spawn "$sub_pool_id" 2>/dev/null; then
            warn "map: orch_spawn failed for sub-pool ${sub_pool_id} (infra failure — aborting)" || true
            infra_failed=true
            break
        fi

        batch_plugins=()
        # #1312 (Copilot): advance batch_start to the next UNPROCESSED index (i),
        # NOT by a fixed max_parallel stride. When orch_dispatch fails, batch_dispatched
        # does not increment, so the inner loop consumes more than max_parallel indices;
        # a fixed stride would then re-process or skip units. `batch_start=i` after the
        # loop guarantees every unit is dispatched exactly once.
        local batch_dispatched=0 i
        for (( i = batch_start; i < total_wu && batch_dispatched < max_parallel; i++ )); do
            wu="${wu_list[$i]}"
            orch_dispatch "$sub_pool_id" "$wu" >/dev/null || {
                warn "map: orch_dispatch failed for work unit at index $i" || true
                fail_count=$(( fail_count + 1 ))
                continue
            }
            batch_dispatched=$(( batch_dispatched + 1 ))
            batch_plugins+=("${plugin_list[$i]}")
        done
        batch_start=$i

        if [[ $batch_dispatched -gt 0 ]]; then
            local collect_rc=0
            _ORCH_COLLECT_OUTCOME=""
            orch_collect "$sub_pool_id" || collect_rc=$?

            if [[ $collect_rc -eq 0 ]]; then
                success_count=$(( success_count + 1 ))
                # #1906: artifact enforcement already ran per work unit inside
                # plugin_hook_call (scan_plugin_outputs).
            elif [[ "${_ORCH_COLLECT_OUTCOME:-}" == "partial" ]]; then
                success_count=$(( success_count + 1 ))
                fail_count=$(( fail_count + 1 ))
            else
                fail_count=$(( fail_count + 1 ))
            fi
        fi

        orch_shutdown "$sub_pool_id" 2>/dev/null || true
    done

    _strategy_cleanup_work_units "${wu_list[@]+"${wu_list[@]}"}"
    # Shut down the original pool_id (caller spawned it; we use sub-pools per batch
    # but the caller's pool must still be closed via orch_shutdown for contract compliance).
    orch_shutdown "$pool_id" 2>/dev/null || true

    # #1312 (Copilot): infra failure (orch_spawn) fails closed — non-zero rc, NOT
    # subject to on_member_error. rc=6 is distinct from member outcomes (0/1/2) so
    # the runner surfaces it as a real failure even under on_member_error=continue.
    if $infra_failed; then
        _ZB_STRATEGY_OUTCOME="infra_failed"
        return 1
    fi

    # #1312: on_member_error=collect (default) — propagate failure outward (group
    # fails if any element failed). runner.sh's strategy: map/map:* call sites rely
    # on this default. on_member_error=continue mirrors parallel_group_run: all
    # elements run regardless of failures; group returns 0 even on partial/all-fail.
    #
    # #1312 (Copilot): unknown on_member_error values are NOT validated — they fall
    # through to the collect branch below (the more CONSERVATIVE default). This
    # matches parallel_group_run, which also does not validate: it only special-cases
    # its recognised enum (`== "collect"`) and treats anything else as its own safe
    # default (parallel-orchestrator.sh:317). Neither path fails loud on a typo. Map
    # deliberately picks collect (not continue) as the fall-through so a typo cannot
    # accidentally make a group non-blocking — safer to over-report than to swallow
    # a failure. (parallel defaults empty→continue; map defaults empty→collect per
    # its strategy: call-site contract, but both fall through to their safe default.)
    if [[ "$on_member_error" == "continue" ]]; then
        _ZB_STRATEGY_OUTCOME="ok"
        return 0
    fi

    if   [[ $fail_count -eq 0 ]];    then _ZB_STRATEGY_OUTCOME="ok"; return 0
    elif [[ $success_count -gt 0 ]]; then _ZB_STRATEGY_OUTCOME="partial"; return 1
    else                                  _ZB_STRATEGY_OUTCOME="failed"; return 1
    fi
}

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# core/pipeline/strategies/sequential.sh — serialized per-platform dispatch (issue #200/#222)
# ADR-009: platforms run one at a time; always halts on the first collect failure.
# Depends on core/orch/contract.sh being sourced first by the caller (runner.sh).
# Sourced library: inherits caller's pipefail; do not add set -euo pipefail here.

[[ -n "${_ZBUILD_STRATEGY_SEQUENTIAL_LOADED:-}" ]] && return 0
_ZBUILD_STRATEGY_SEQUENTIAL_LOADED=1

_ZBUILD_STRATEGIES_DIR_SEQ="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)"
source "${_ZBUILD_STRATEGIES_DIR_SEQ}/common.sh"

# ─── _strategy_run_sequential ────────────────────────────────────────────────
# Usage: _strategy_run_sequential <pool_id> <stage> <roles_out> <state_file> <plugins_root>
#   pool_id    — caller-supplied, already validated
#   stage      — stage name

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# core/pipeline/strategies/fanout.sh — parallel per-platform dispatch (issue #198/#222)
# ADR-009: all platforms run concurrently; stage succeeds iff all succeed (rc=2 = partial).
# Depends on core/orch/contract.sh being sourced first by the caller (runner.sh).
# Sourced library: inherits caller's pipefail; do not add set -euo pipefail here.

[[ -n "${_ZBUILD_STRATEGY_FANOUT_LOADED:-}" ]] && return 0
_ZBUILD_STRATEGY_FANOUT_LOADED=1

_ZBUILD_STRATEGIES_DIR_FANOUT="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)"
source "${_ZBUILD_STRATEGIES_DIR_FANOUT}/common.sh"

# ─── _strategy_run_fanout ────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# Usage: _strategy_run_fanout <pool_id> <stage> <roles_out> <state_file> <plugins_root>
#   pool_id    — caller-supplied, already validated (no orch_spawn called here)
#   stage      — stage name (e.g. "intake")
#   roles_out  — newline-delimited list of role names
#   state_file — path to pipeline state file
#   plugins_root — path to plugins directory
#
# Dispatches one work unit per role×platform pair in parallel via orch_dispatch.
# Collects all results with orch_collect.
# Calls orch_shutdown and cleans up work units on both success and failure paths.
#
# Returns:
#   0 — all succeeded
#   1 — all failed (collect failure with no successes)
#   2 — partial (at least one success, at least one fail); callers treat as stage fail
#   4 — no plugin found for any role (caller may fall back to stage-id lookup)
_strategy_run_fanout() {
    # #1850 (ADR-054 §4): rc is 0 or 1; WHY rides this word, which the caller
    # reads in the same shell — ok | partial | empty | no_plugin | bad_dimension
    # | infra_failed | failed.
    _ZB_STRATEGY_OUTCOME="failed"
    local pool_id="$1" stage="$2" roles_out="$3" state_file="$4" plugins_root="$5"
    local success_count=0 fail_count=0 any_plugin_found=false dispatch_count=0
    local -a work_units=() dispatched_plugins=()

    local role platform plugin_dir wu
    while IFS= read -r role; do
        [[ -z "$role" ]] && continue
        for platform in "${_DETECTED_PLATFORMS[@]}"; do
            # Intentional fail-open: resolver returns "" when no match — skip silently.
            plugin_dir="$(resolve_plugin_for_role "$role" "$platform" "$plugins_root" 2>/dev/null || true)"
            [[ -z "$plugin_dir" ]] && \
                plugin_dir="$(resolve_plugin_for_role "$role" "" "$plugins_root" 2>/dev/null || true)"
            [[ -z "$plugin_dir" ]] && continue
            any_plugin_found=true

            wu="$(_strategy_make_work_unit "$plugin_dir" "$stage" "$state_file" "$platform")" || {
                warn "fanout: failed to create work unit for role=$role platform=$platform" || true
                fail_count=$((fail_count + 1))
                continue
            }
            work_units+=("$wu")

            orch_dispatch "$pool_id" "$wu" >/dev/null || {
                warn "fanout: orch_dispatch failed for role=$role platform=$platform" || true
                fail_count=$((fail_count + 1))
                continue
            }
            dispatch_count=$((dispatch_count + 1))
            dispatched_plugins+=("$plugin_dir")
        done
    done <<< "$roles_out"

    if ! $any_plugin_found; then
        _strategy_cleanup_work_units "${work_units[@]+"${work_units[@]}"}"
        orch_shutdown "$pool_id" 2>/dev/null || true
        _ZB_STRATEGY_OUTCOME="no_plugin"
        return 1
    fi

    # Only collect if at least one dispatch succeeded; otherwise pool is empty
    # and orch_collect would return 0 (no results) — misreported as success.
    if [[ "$dispatch_count" -gt 0 ]]; then
        local collect_rc=0
        _ORCH_COLLECT_OUTCOME=""
        orch_collect "$pool_id" || collect_rc=$?

        # orch_collect: 0 = all passed; 1 otherwise, partial named on
        # _ORCH_COLLECT_OUTCOME (#1850 — it was rc 2).
        if [[ $collect_rc -eq 0 ]]; then
            success_count=$((success_count + 1))
            # #1906: no artifact check here. Each work unit calls plugin_hook_call
            # (strategies/common.sh), so scan_plugin_outputs has already enforced
            # every declared output for every dispatched plugin.
        elif [[ "${_ORCH_COLLECT_OUTCOME:-}" == "partial" ]]; then
            success_count=$((success_count + 1))
            fail_count=$((fail_count + 1))
        else
            fail_count=$((fail_count + 1))
        fi
    fi

    _strategy_cleanup_work_units "${work_units[@]+"${work_units[@]}"}"
    orch_shutdown "$pool_id" 2>/dev/null || true

    if   [[ $fail_count -eq 0 ]];    then _ZB_STRATEGY_OUTCOME="ok"; return 0
    elif [[ $success_count -gt 0 ]]; then _ZB_STRATEGY_OUTCOME="partial"; return 1
    else                                  _ZB_STRATEGY_OUTCOME="failed"; return 1
    fi
}

# ─── _strategy_cleanup_work_units ────────────────────────────────────────────
_strategy_cleanup_work_units() {
    [[ $# -eq 0 ]] && return 0
    rm -f "$@" 2>/dev/null || true
}

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# core/pipeline/strategies/map.sh — data-driven map over any declared list dimension (issue #1285)
# ADR-047: generalizes fanout (platforms) to arbitrary declared dimensions.
# When dimension=platforms, behavior is byte-identical to _strategy_run_fanout.
# Sourced library: inherits caller's pipefail; do not add set -euo pipefail here.

[[ -n "${_ZBUILD_STRATEGY_MAP_LOADED:-}" ]] && return 0
_ZBUILD_STRATEGY_MAP_LOADED=1

_ZBUILD_STRATEGIES_DIR_MAP="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)"
source "${_ZBUILD_STRATEGIES_DIR_MAP}/common.sh"

# ─── _strategy_map_resolve_dimension ─────────────────────────────────────────
# Resolves the iteration list for the given dimension name.
# For "platforms": uses _DETECTED_PLATFORMS (set by runner before dispatch).
# For other names: uses _MAP_DIM_<name> array if set; otherwise empty.
# Prints one element per line; no output = empty dimension.
_strategy_map_resolve_dimension() {
    local dim="${1:-platforms}"
    if [[ "$dim" == "platforms" ]]; then
        local p
        for p in "${_DETECTED_PLATFORMS[@]+"${_DETECTED_PLATFORMS[@]}"}"; do
            [[ -n "$p" ]] && printf '%s\n' "$p"
        done
        return 0
    fi
    # Arbitrary dimension: caller must export _MAP_DIM_<name> as an array.
    # Validate dimension name to prevent variable-name injection.
    if [[ ! "$dim" =~ ^[a-zA-Z0-9_]{1,64}$ ]]; then
        warn "map: invalid dimension name: ${dim}" || true
        return 1
    fi
    # Read the caller's _MAP_DIM_<name> array by reference (Bash 5+ floor — see
    # scripts/lib/compat.sh). The name was validated above, guarding the target.
    # The array lives in the caller's scope (same sourced shell). Guarded
    # expansion tolerates an unset target under the caller's `set -u`.
    local -n _ref="_MAP_DIM_${dim}"
    local elem
    for elem in "${_ref[@]+"${_ref[@]}"}"; do
        [[ -n "$elem" ]] && printf '%s\n' "$elem"
    done
}

# ─── _strategy_map_resolve_max ───────────────────────────────────────────────
# Resolves the max_parallel concurrency cap for a map group.
# Input: raw max value from template (_TPL_MAP_MAX_<gid>), e.g. "4", "auto", "".
# Mirrors _parallel_resolve_max (parallel-orchestrator.sh) EXACTLY so map and
# parallel groups agree on the cap and its fail-safe:
#   - explicit positive integer  → used as-is (then capped at _PARALLEL_MAX_JOBS_CAP)
#   - "auto" / empty             → ZBUILD_PARALLEL_JOBS env override, else CPU count
#   - ANYTHING else (non-numeric typo, "0", negative) → CLAMPED TO 1 (fail-safe).
# #1312 (Copilot): an invalid template value must NOT silently remove the cap by
# falling through to CPU-count concurrency — that is the opposite of safe. Clamp to 1.
_strategy_map_resolve_max() {
    local raw="${1:-}"
    # #1312 (Copilot): reuse the parallel path's readonly cap so map and parallel
    # stay in sync if it ever changes — don't duplicate the literal. Falls back to 8
    # only when map.sh is sourced standalone (unit tests) without the parallel module.
    local cap="${_PARALLEL_MAX_JOBS_CAP:-8}"
    local max="$raw"
    # "auto" is an explicit request for the CPU-based default (map-specific alias);
    # normalise it to empty so the empty-branch resolves the default.
    [[ "$max" == "auto" ]] && max=""
    if [[ -z "$max" ]]; then
        if [[ "${ZBUILD_PARALLEL_JOBS:-}" =~ ^[1-9][0-9]*$ ]]; then
            max="$ZBUILD_PARALLEL_JOBS"
        else
            max="$( { nproc 2>/dev/null || sysctl -n hw.ncpu 2>/dev/null; } | head -1 )"  # sigpipe-ok: writer emits exactly one line
            [[ "$max" =~ ^[1-9][0-9]*$ ]] || max=4
        fi
    fi
    # Fail-safe clamp: any non-positive-integer (typo, "0", negative) → 1.
    [[ "$max" =~ ^[1-9][0-9]*$ ]] || max=1
    (( max > cap )) && max=$cap
    printf '%s' "$max"
}

# ─── _strategy_run_map ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# Usage: _strategy_run_map <pool_id> <stage> <roles_out> <state_file> <plugins_root> \
#                          [dimension] [env_target] [max_parallel] [on_member_error]
#   pool_id          — caller-supplied, already validated. Used as the base for
#                      per-batch sub-pool ids ("<base>-b<N>", truncated to fit the
#                      64-char backend limit). The FIFO-batch loop below spawns and
#                      shuts down one sub-pool per batch via orch_spawn/orch_shutdown;
#                      the caller's own pool_id is also orch_shutdown at the end.
#   stage            — stage name (e.g. "intake")
#   roles_out        — newline-delimited list of role names
#   state_file       — path to pipeline state file
#   plugins_root     — path to plugins directory
#   dimension        — list name to iterate (default: "platforms")
#   env_target       — optional env var name to set to each element per work unit
#                      (issue #1295, ADR-047 §2: generic dimension→env mapping declared
#                      by the template's `as:` field; empty = no extra env). The
#                      strategy is element-name-agnostic — it never hardcodes a var name.
#   max_parallel     — concurrency cap (issue #1312): "auto"/empty = CPU-based cap;
#                      integer = explicit cap. Enforced via a FIFO-pool batch loop
#                      (mirrors ADR-039 parallel_group_run FIFO pool semantics).
#   on_member_error  — "collect" (default) or "continue" (issue #1312).
#                      continue: a failing element does NOT abort the group (return 0);
#                      collect:  any failure is propagated (return 1/2).
#                      Unknown values are NOT validated — they fall through to collect
#                      (the conservative default), matching parallel_group_run which
#                      also silently defaults unknown values to its safe branch.
#                      Mirrors parallel_group_run on_member_error semantics (ADR-039).
#
# Dispatches one work unit per role×element pair.
# When dimension=platforms, behavior is byte-identical to _strategy_run_fanout.
#
# Returns:
#   0 — all succeeded, OR on_member_error=continue (even with failures)
#   1 — all failed (only when on_member_error=collect)
#   2 — partial (at least one success, at least one fail; only when on_member_error=collect)
#   3 — empty dimension (no elements to iterate; caller/runner maps to no-op 0)
#   4 — no plugin found for any role
#   5 — invalid/unknown dimension name (fail-closed; runner surfaces as failure)
#   6 — infrastructure failure (orch_spawn failed for a batch sub-pool). Fail-closed:
#       NOT subject to on_member_error — an infra failure is never a member outcome.
#   Two members that would run under one unit name (#1706) are refused before
#   any member starts: rc 1 (ADR-054 §4 — rc says only "failed"); the
#   strategy.unit_name_conflict event says why. Not subject to on_member_error.
# _map_unit_element <var> <role_count> <role> <element> — sets <var> to the part
# of a member's unit name after the stage (#1706): the element, or
# <role>.<element> when the map runs more than one role. No subshell per member.
_map_unit_element() {
    if [[ "$2" -gt 1 ]]; then printf -v "$1" '%s.%s' "$3" "$4"; else printf -v "$1" '%s' "$4"; fi
}

_strategy_run_map() {
    # #1850 (ADR-054 §4): rc is 0 or 1; WHY rides this word, which the caller
    # reads in the same shell — ok | partial | empty | no_plugin | bad_dimension
    # | infra_failed | failed.
    _ZB_STRATEGY_OUTCOME="failed"
    local pool_id="$1" stage="$2" roles_out="$3" state_file="$4" plugins_root="$5"
    local dimension="${6:-platforms}" env_target="${7:-}"
    local max_raw="${8:-}" on_member_error="${9:-collect}"
    local success_count=0 fail_count=0 any_plugin_found=false

    # Resolve the iteration list. Capture output AND rc explicitly — a process
    # substitution would discard the resolver's status, collapsing an invalid
    # dimension (rc=2) into the empty path (rc=3) and masking a fail-closed error.
    local _resolved _res_rc
    _resolved="$(_strategy_map_resolve_dimension "$dimension")"; _res_rc=$?
    if [[ $_res_rc -ne 0 ]]; then
        # Invalid/unknown dimension name — fail closed. Distinct from empty (rc=3);
        # the runner does NOT map rc=5 to 0, so this surfaces as a real failure.
        orch_shutdown "$pool_id" 2>/dev/null || true
        _ZB_STRATEGY_OUTCOME="bad_dimension"
        return 1
    fi

    local -a elements=()
    local _elem
    while IFS= read -r _elem; do
        [[ -n "$_elem" ]] && elements+=("$_elem")
    done <<< "$_resolved"

    if [[ ${#elements[@]} -eq 0 ]]; then
        orch_shutdown "$pool_id" 2>/dev/null || true
        _ZB_STRATEGY_OUTCOME="empty"
        return 0
    fi

    # #1312: resolve the concurrency cap (mirrors ADR-039 FIFO pool).
    local max_parallel
    max_parallel="$(_strategy_map_resolve_max "$max_raw")"

    # #1706 (ADR-054 §3.1): every member runs under <stage>.<element>. Two
    # members with one name would write the same records at the same time, so
    # the group is refused before any member starts.
    # With more than one role every role runs on every element, so the role is
    # part of the name: <stage>.<role>.<element>.
    local -A _unit_seen=()
    local _u_role _u_elem _u_name _u_roles=0
    while IFS= read -r _u_role; do [[ -n "$_u_role" ]] && _u_roles=$((_u_roles + 1)); done <<< "$roles_out"
    while IFS= read -r _u_role; do
        [[ -z "$_u_role" ]] && continue
        for _u_elem in "${elements[@]}"; do
            _map_unit_element _u_name "$_u_roles" "$_u_role" "$_u_elem"; _u_name="${stage}.${_u_name}"
            if [[ -n "${_unit_seen[$_u_name]:-}" ]]; then
                warn "map: two members of '$stage' would both run as '$_u_name' — refusing the group" || true
                eb_emit_event "strategy.unit_name_conflict" "stage=$stage" "unit=$_u_name" 2>/dev/null || true
                orch_shutdown "$pool_id" 2>/dev/null || true
                return 1
            fi
            _unit_seen[$_u_name]=1
        done
    done <<< "$roles_out"

    # Build the ordered list of (plugin_dir, element) work items by iterating
    # roles × elements — same order as before, just collected before dispatch.
    local -a wu_list=() plugin_list=()
    local role element plugin_dir wu
    while IFS= read -r role; do
        [[ -z "$role" ]] && continue
        for element in "${elements[@]}"; do
            # Mirror fanout.sh platform-specific then generic resolution.
            plugin_dir="$(resolve_plugin_for_role "$role" "$element" "$plugins_root" 2>/dev/null || true)"
            [[ -z "$plugin_dir" ]] && \
                plugin_dir="$(resolve_plugin_for_role "$role" "" "$plugins_root" 2>/dev/null || true)"
            [[ -z "$plugin_dir" ]] && continue
            any_plugin_found=true

            # Only the platforms dimension populates ZBUILD_PLATFORM (ADR-009 §6
            # env contract) — pass the element as the 4th arg so the platforms
            # path stays byte-identical to fanout. For non-platform dimensions
            # (lenses/mutants), pass the generic element identity via args 5+6
            # (ZBUILD_MAP_ELEMENT / ZBUILD_MAP_DIMENSION, issue #1295, ADR-047 §2)
            # so each work unit is distinguishable without hijacking ZBUILD_PLATFORM.
            # An optional env_target (arg 7, from the template's `as:`) additionally
            # sets a named env var to the element — a generic mapping the strategy
            # applies without knowing which dimension or var it is.
            _map_unit_element _u_elem "$_u_roles" "$role" "$element"
            if [[ "$dimension" == "platforms" ]]; then
                wu="$(_strategy_make_work_unit "$plugin_dir" "$stage" "$state_file" "$element" "" "" "" "$_u_elem")"
            else
                wu="$(_strategy_make_work_unit "$plugin_dir" "$stage" "$state_file" "generic" "$element" "$dimension" "$env_target" "$_u_elem")"
            fi || {
                warn "map: failed to create work unit for role=$role element=$element" || true
                fail_count=$((fail_count + 1))
                continue
            }
            wu_list+=("$wu")
            plugin_list+=("$plugin_dir")
        done
    done <<< "$roles_out"

    if ! $any_plugin_found; then
        _strategy_cleanup_work_units "${wu_list[@]+"${wu_list[@]}"}"
        orch_shutdown "$pool_id" 2>/dev/null || true
        _ZB_STRATEGY_OUTCOME="no_plugin"
        return 1
    fi

    # #1312: FIFO-pool batch dispatch — respects max_parallel cap (ADR-039 model).
    # Dispatch up to max_parallel work units per batch; collect before advancing.
    # This enforces the concurrency cap via the orch backend's own pool machinery.
    # Each batch uses a sub-pool so collect drains only the in-flight batch.
    # on_member_error=continue: all batches run regardless of prior batch failures.
    local total_wu="${#wu_list[@]}"
    local batch_start=0 batch_seq=0
    local infra_failed=false   # #1312: orch_spawn failure = infra error → fail-closed
    local -a batch_plugins=()
    # #1312 (Copilot): backends validate pool_id against ^[a-zA-Z0-9_-]{1,64}$.
    # The per-batch "-b<N>" suffix must not push the id past 64 chars, or orch_spawn
    # fails and the whole batch is silently skipped. Keep the base ≤54 chars so
    # "<base>-b<N>" always fits (reserve 10 for the largest realistic suffix, e.g.
    # "-b99999999").
    #
    # #1312 (Copilot): collision-safe truncation. Real pool_ids put their UNIQUE
    # tail last ("map-<gid>-$$", "zbuild-<stage>-$$-<ns>"), so a plain prefix
    # truncation would drop exactly the disambiguating suffix — two distinct bases
    # sharing a 54-char prefix would collide into the same sub-pool dir. Instead,
    # when over-long, keep a readable 45-char prefix + an 8-char hash of the FULL
    # pool_id (45 + 1 + 8 = 54), so distinct bases yield distinct sub-pool bases.
    local _sub_pool_base="$pool_id"
    if [[ ${#_sub_pool_base} -gt 54 ]]; then
        local _pid_hash
        _pid_hash="$(printf '%s' "$pool_id" | shasum -a 256 2>/dev/null | cut -c1-8)"
        # Fallback if shasum is unavailable: cksum (POSIX) → hex-ish digits.
        [[ -n "$_pid_hash" ]] || _pid_hash="$(printf '%s' "$pool_id" | cksum | cut -c1-8)"
        _sub_pool_base="${pool_id:0:45}-${_pid_hash}"
    fi
    while [[ $batch_start -lt $total_wu ]]; do
        batch_seq=$(( batch_seq + 1 ))
        local sub_pool_id="${_sub_pool_base}-b${batch_seq}"

        # #1312 (Copilot): orch_spawn failure is an INFRASTRUCTURE failure, NOT a
        # member failure — silently skipping a batch's work units (and possibly
        # still returning 0 under on_member_error=continue) hides real breakage.
        # Fail closed: stop dispatching and propagate a non-zero rc regardless of
        # on_member_error.
        if ! orch_spawn "$sub_pool_id" 2>/dev/null; then
            warn "map: orch_spawn failed for sub-pool ${sub_pool_id} (infra failure — aborting)" || true
            infra_failed=true
            break
        fi

        batch_plugins=()
        # #1312 (Copilot): advance batch_start to the next UNPROCESSED index (i),
        # NOT by a fixed max_parallel stride. When orch_dispatch fails, batch_dispatched
        # does not increment, so the inner loop consumes more than max_parallel indices;
        # a fixed stride would then re-process or skip units. `batch_start=i` after the
        # loop guarantees every unit is dispatched exactly once.
        local batch_dispatched=0 i
        for (( i = batch_start; i < total_wu && batch_dispatched < max_parallel; i++ )); do
            wu="${wu_list[$i]}"
            orch_dispatch "$sub_pool_id" "$wu" >/dev/null || {
                warn "map: orch_dispatch failed for work unit at index $i" || true
                fail_count=$(( fail_count + 1 ))
                continue
            }
            batch_dispatched=$(( batch_dispatched + 1 ))
            batch_plugins+=("${plugin_list[$i]}")
        done
        batch_start=$i

        if [[ $batch_dispatched -gt 0 ]]; then
            local collect_rc=0
            _ORCH_COLLECT_OUTCOME=""
            orch_collect "$sub_pool_id" || collect_rc=$?

            if [[ $collect_rc -eq 0 ]]; then
                success_count=$(( success_count + 1 ))
                # #1906: artifact enforcement already ran per work unit inside
                # plugin_hook_call (scan_plugin_outputs).
            elif [[ "${_ORCH_COLLECT_OUTCOME:-}" == "partial" ]]; then
                success_count=$(( success_count + 1 ))
                fail_count=$(( fail_count + 1 ))
            else
                fail_count=$(( fail_count + 1 ))
            fi
        fi

        orch_shutdown "$sub_pool_id" 2>/dev/null || true
    done

    _strategy_cleanup_work_units "${wu_list[@]+"${wu_list[@]}"}"
    # Shut down the original pool_id (caller spawned it; we use sub-pools per batch
    # but the caller's pool must still be closed via orch_shutdown for contract compliance).
    orch_shutdown "$pool_id" 2>/dev/null || true

    # #1312 (Copilot): infra failure (orch_spawn) fails closed — non-zero rc, NOT
    # subject to on_member_error. rc=6 is distinct from member outcomes (0/1/2) so
    # the runner surfaces it as a real failure even under on_member_error=continue.
    if $infra_failed; then
        _ZB_STRATEGY_OUTCOME="infra_failed"
        return 1
    fi

    # #1312: on_member_error=collect (default) — propagate failure outward (group
    # fails if any element failed). runner.sh's strategy: map/map:* call sites rely
    # on this default. on_member_error=continue mirrors parallel_group_run: all
    # elements run regardless of failures; group returns 0 even on partial/all-fail.
    #
    # #1312 (Copilot): unknown on_member_error values are NOT validated — they fall
    # through to the collect branch below (the more CONSERVATIVE default). This
    # matches parallel_group_run, which also does not validate: it only special-cases
    # its recognised enum (`== "collect"`) and treats anything else as its own safe
    # default (parallel-orchestrator.sh:317). Neither path fails loud on a typo. Map
    # deliberately picks collect (not continue) as the fall-through so a typo cannot
    # accidentally make a group non-blocking — safer to over-report than to swallow
    # a failure. (parallel defaults empty→continue; map defaults empty→collect per
    # its strategy: call-site contract, but both fall through to their safe default.)
    if [[ "$on_member_error" == "continue" ]]; then
        _ZB_STRATEGY_OUTCOME="ok"
        return 0
    fi

    if   [[ $fail_count -eq 0 ]];    then _ZB_STRATEGY_OUTCOME="ok"; return 0
    elif [[ $success_count -gt 0 ]]; then _ZB_STRATEGY_OUTCOME="partial"; return 1
    else                                  _ZB_STRATEGY_OUTCOME="failed"; return 1
    fi

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# core/pipeline/strategies/sequential.sh — serialized per-platform dispatch (issue #200/#222)
# ADR-009: platforms run one at a time; always halts on the first collect failure.
# Depends on core/orch/contract.sh being sourced first by the caller (runner.sh).
# Sourced library: inherits caller's pipefail; do not add set -euo pipefail here.

[[ -n "${_ZBUILD_STRATEGY_SEQUENTIAL_LOADED:-}" ]] && return 0
_ZBUILD_STRATEGY_SEQUENTIAL_LOADED=1

_ZBUILD_STRATEGIES_DIR_SEQ="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)"
source "${_ZBUILD_STRATEGIES_DIR_SEQ}/common.sh"

# ─── _strategy_run_sequential ────────────────────────────────────────────────
# Usage: _strategy_run_sequential <pool_id> <stage> <roles_out> <state_file> <plugins_root>
#   pool_id    — caller-supplied, already validated
#   stage      — stage name
#   roles_out  — newline-delimited list of role names
#   state_file — path to pipeline state file
#   plugins_root — path to plugins directory
#
# Dispatches one work unit at a time via orch_dispatch + orch_collect.
# Halts on first failure (does not continue to next platform/role).
# Always calls orch_shutdown on exit (success or failure).
# Artifact enforcement happens per work unit inside plugin_hook_call (#1906).
#
# Returns:
#   0 — all succeeded
#   1 — any collect/dispatch failure
#   4 — no plugin found for any role (caller may fall back to stage-id lookup)
_strategy_run_sequential() {
    # #1850 (ADR-054 §4): rc is 0 or 1; WHY rides this word, which the caller
    # reads in the same shell — ok | partial | empty | no_plugin | bad_dimension
    # | infra_failed | failed.
    _ZB_STRATEGY_OUTCOME="failed"
    local pool_id="$1" stage="$2" roles_out="$3" state_file="$4" plugins_root="$5"
    local any_plugin_found=false

    local role platform plugin_dir wu prc
    while IFS= read -r role; do
        [[ -z "$role" ]] && continue
        for platform in "${_DETECTED_PLATFORMS[@]}"; do
            plugin_dir="$(resolve_plugin_for_role "$role" "$platform" "$plugins_root" 2>/dev/null || true)"
            [[ -z "$plugin_dir" ]] && \
                plugin_dir="$(resolve_plugin_for_role "$role" "" "$plugins_root" 2>/dev/null || true)"
            [[ -z "$plugin_dir" ]] && continue
            any_plugin_found=true

            wu="$(_strategy_make_work_unit "$plugin_dir" "$stage" "$state_file" "$platform")" || {
                warn "sequential: failed to create work unit for role=$role platform=$platform" || true
                orch_shutdown "$pool_id" 2>/dev/null || true
                return 1
            }

            orch_dispatch "$pool_id" "$wu" >/dev/null || {
                warn "sequential: orch_dispatch failed for role=$role platform=$platform" || true
                rm -f "$wu" 2>/dev/null || true
                orch_shutdown "$pool_id" 2>/dev/null || true
                return 1
            }

            prc=0
            orch_collect "$pool_id" || prc=$?
            rm -f "$wu" 2>/dev/null || true

            if [[ $prc -ne 0 ]]; then
                warn "sequential: stage=$stage role=$role platform=$platform failed (rc=$prc)" || true
                orch_shutdown "$pool_id" 2>/dev/null || true
                return 1
            fi

        done
    done <<< "$roles_out"

    orch_shutdown "$pool_id" 2>/dev/null || true
    $any_plugin_found || { _ZB_STRATEGY_OUTCOME="no_plugin"; return 1; }
    _ZB_STRATEGY_OUTCOME="ok"
    return 0
}

1	#!/usr/bin/env bash
2	# [#1801/SPEC-7] Guard: removing ZBUILD_ORCH_TIMEOUT from the three strategy files
3	# means the per-dispatch watchdog is the only stage time limit.
4	#
5	# Before this change the strategy files had `orch_collect … --timeout
6	# "${ZBUILD_ORCH_TIMEOUT:-300}"` as a flat ceiling; a plan dispatch running
7	# longer than 300 s would have been killed even when its `stage_timeout_s`
8	# allowed more. After the change, orch_collect is called without --timeout (or
9	# with no ceiling), leaving the per-dispatch watchdog in lifecycle.sh as the
10	# only limit.
11	#
12	# The assertions are source-level: they verify that each strategy file no
13	# longer carries the flat ceiling. This test FAILS on pre-change code
14	# (where ZBUILD_ORCH_TIMEOUT still appears) and PASSES after the change.
15	set -euo pipefail
16	
17	SCRIPT_DIR="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)"
18	REPO_ROOT="$(cd "$SCRIPT_DIR/../.." && pwd)"
19	
20	# shellcheck source=../../scripts/lib/helpers.sh
21	source "$REPO_ROOT/scripts/lib/helpers.sh"
22	# shellcheck source=../../scripts/lib/test-helpers.sh
23	source "$REPO_ROOT/scripts/lib/test-helpers.sh"
24	
25	print_test_header "[#1801/SPEC-7] ZBUILD_ORCH_TIMEOUT absent from strategy files"
26	
27	# ─── Each strategy file must not reference ZBUILD_ORCH_TIMEOUT ───────────────
28	# These are the three files the design names: fanout.sh, sequential.sh, map.sh.
29	# Every occurrence of ZBUILD_ORCH_TIMEOUT pins a flat ceiling that the per-dispatch
30	# watchdog is meant to replace.
31	
32	for _sf in \
33	    core/pipeline/strategies/fanout.sh \
34	    core/pipeline/strategies/sequential.sh \
35	    core/pipeline/strategies/map.sh; do
36	
37	    _file="$REPO_ROOT/$_sf"
38	    if [[ ! -f "$_file" ]]; then
39	        assert_fail "[#1801/SPEC-7] $_sf exists" "file not found: $_file"
40	        continue
41	    fi
42	
43	    if grep -q 'ZBUILD_ORCH_TIMEOUT' "$_file"; then
44	        assert_fail "[#1801/SPEC-7] $_sf carries no ZBUILD_ORCH_TIMEOUT flat ceiling" \
45	            "ZBUILD_ORCH_TIMEOUT still present — a plan dispatch longer than the default 300 s" \
46	            "would be killed before its stage_timeout_s expires"
47	    else
48	        assert_pass "[#1801/SPEC-7] $_sf carries no ZBUILD_ORCH_TIMEOUT flat ceiling"
49	    fi
50	
51	    # Also verify orch_collect/orch_wait calls carry no --timeout flag.
52	    # A hard-coded --timeout N in the orch call would impose a flat ceiling
53	    # independent of ZBUILD_ORCH_TIMEOUT and would kill long-but-valid dispatches.
54	    if grep -qE 'orch_collect.*--timeout|orch_wait.*--timeout' "$_file"; then
55	        assert_fail "[#1801/SPEC-7] $_sf orch_collect/orch_wait carry no --timeout flag" \
56	            "--timeout found in orch call — imposes a flat ceiling that overrides stage_timeout_s"
57	    else
58	        assert_pass "[#1801/SPEC-7] $_sf orch_collect/orch_wait carry no --timeout flag"
59	    fi
60	done
61	
62	print_test_results
63	exit $((FAIL > 0))

9	# name in the reason.

12	# back instead of failing) and PASS after the change.

21	source "$REPO_ROOT/scripts/lib/test-helpers.sh"

24	setup_test_env "orch-backend-misconfigured"

36	        source "'"$REPO_ROOT"'/core/orch/contract.sh" 2>/dev/null || true

38	        echo "exit:$?"
39	    ' 2>&1)" || _rc1=$?

42	# backend name appears in the message.

44	        && grep -q 'no-such-backend' <<< "$_out1"; then

66	    fi
