1	#!/usr/bin/env bash
2	# Integration test (#1829, ADR-054 §7): the runner dispatches cleanup(release)
3	# on EVERY exit path from a run — success, non-zero rc, the SIGINT propagation
4	# chain, an external SIGTERM, and an external timeout.
5	#
6	# This is the acceptance criterion the mechanism exists for: a stage's live
7	# resources must be freed however the run ends. A single missed exit path leaks
8	# whatever that stage spawned (#1748: suites observed alive 15+ min after exit).
9	#
10	# Why SIGINT is driven by the stage rather than `kill -INT`: this harness starts
11	# non-interactively with SIGINT inherited as SIG_IGN, and POSIX forbids a child
12	# from un-ignoring it — so `kill -INT` is silently dropped and the assertion
13	# would pass standalone while proving nothing. The repo's existing
14	# sigint-aborts-pipeline-test.sh drives the same chain the same way: the child
15	# returns 130, which is exactly what the kernel produces on Ctrl-C. Since #1850
16	# (ADR-054 §4, ADR-025) a signal is a recorded WORD, not an rc, so the stage
17	# also arms the abort sentinel (empty = sigint), as the runner's INT trap in
18	# the process group would.
19	#
20	# Assertion in every case: the stub stages' cleanup hooks recorded `release`
21	# (and never `purge`) in the marker file.
22	set -euo pipefail
23	
24	SCRIPT_DIR="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)"
25	REPO_ROOT="$(cd "$SCRIPT_DIR/../.." && pwd)"
26	RUNNER="$REPO_ROOT/core/pipeline/runner.sh"
27	
28	# shellcheck source=../../scripts/lib/helpers.sh
29	source "$REPO_ROOT/scripts/lib/helpers.sh"
30	# shellcheck source=../../scripts/lib/test-helpers.sh
31	source "$REPO_ROOT/scripts/lib/test-helpers.sh"
32	
33	print_test_header "runner dispatches cleanup(release) on every exit path (#1829)"
34	setup_test_env "runner-release-exit-paths"
35	export ZBUILD_CONTRACT_VALIDATOR=warn
36	
37	PLUGINS_ROOT="$TEST_TEMP_DIR/plugins"
38	export ZBUILD_PLUGINS_ROOT="$PLUGINS_ROOT"
39	export ZBUILD_EVENT_SCHEMA="$REPO_ROOT/config/event-schema.json"
40	export ZBUILD_MODELS_FILE="$REPO_ROOT/config/models.json"
41	export ZBUILD_CYCLES_ENABLED=0
42	mkdir -p "$PLUGINS_ROOT"
43	
44	# The teardown plugin resolves its repo root by walking three levels up from
45	# its own directory (plugin-bootstrap), using a LOGICAL pwd — so symlinking the
46	# plugin itself would resolve to TEST_TEMP_DIR and fail to find helpers.sh.
47	# Give TEST_TEMP_DIR the shape of a repo root instead, then copy teardown in.
48	ln -s "$REPO_ROOT/scripts" "$TEST_TEMP_DIR/scripts"
49	ln -s "$REPO_ROOT/core"    "$TEST_TEMP_DIR/core"
50	mkdir -p "$PLUGINS_ROOT/tool"
51	cp -R "$REPO_ROOT/plugins/tool/teardown" "$PLUGINS_ROOT/tool/teardown"
52	
53	mock_plugin_factory "intake" "agent" 0 >/dev/null
54	mock_plugin_factory "build"  "agent" 0 >/dev/null
55	mock_plugin_factory "test"   "tool"  0 >/dev/null
56	
57	# Declare the optional cleanup hook — without it plugin_hook_call emits
58	# `plugin.cleanup.absent`, returns 0 (#1823: rc is binary), and the stage is a
59	# no-op rather than a witness.
60	# Re-emit the manifest rather than appending: `cleanup:` has to sit inside the
61	# contiguous `hooks:` block, and mock_plugin_factory already wrote `requires:`
62	# after it. #1850: the re-emitted manifest keeps the factory's v2 declaration —
63	# result_contract 2 and a JSON primary each run hook below writes.
64	for _spec in "agent/intake:intake:intake_cleanup" "agent/build:build:build_cleanup" "tool/test:test:test_cleanup"; do
65	    _dir="${_spec%%:*}"; _rest="${_spec#*:}"; _id="${_rest%%:*}"; _fn="${_rest#*:}"
66	    _kind="${_dir%%/*}"
67	    cat > "$PLUGINS_ROOT/$_dir/manifest.yaml" <<EOF
68	id: $_id
69	name: Test $_id
70	kind: $_kind
71	version: 0.0.1
72	hooks:
73	  run: ${_id//-/_}_run
74	  cleanup: $_fn
75	requires:
76	  core:
77	    - redaction
78	provides:
79	  result_contract: 2
80	outputs:
81	  - id: ${_id//-/_}_result
82	    path: \${artifact_dir}/${_id}-result.json
83	    type: ${_id}-result.json@1
84	    format: json
85	    required: true
86	    primary: true
87	config:
88	  valid_verdicts: [pass, error]
89	EOF
90	done
91	
92	# Stubs: run honours env-driven rc/sleep; cleanup records "<stage>:<scope>".
93	cat > "$PLUGINS_ROOT/agent/intake/plugin.sh" <<'PLUG'
94	intake_run() {
95	    local _art; _art="${ZBUILD_ARTIFACT_DIR:-$(dirname "$2")/artifacts}"; mkdir -p "$_art"
96	    printf '%s' '{"result_contract":2,"verdict":"pass","disposition":"complete","reason":"stub"}' > "$_art/intake-result.json"
97	    return 0
98	}
99	intake_cleanup() { printf 'intake:%s\n' "${3:-NOSCOPE}" >> "${RELEASE_MARKER}"; return 0; }
100	PLUG
101	cat > "$PLUGINS_ROOT/agent/build/plugin.sh" <<'PLUG'
102	build_run() {
103	    : > "${BUILD_STARTED:-/dev/null}"
104	    if [[ "${BUILD_SLEEP:-0}" == "1" ]]; then
105	        local _i; for _i in $(seq 1 300); do sleep 0.1; done
106	    fi
107	    if [[ "${BUILD_RUN_SPAWN_IGNORE_TERM:-0}" == "1" ]]; then
108	        # Spawn a child that ignores TERM and records its PID — used to verify
109	        # that an external SIGTERM to the runner kills the run hook's process group.
110	        ( trap '' TERM; printf '%s\n' "$BASHPID" >> "${BUILD_STARTED%/*}/run-child.pid"; sleep 120 ) &
111	        local _j; for _j in $(seq 1 300); do sleep 0.1; done
112	    fi
113	    local _art; _art="${ZBUILD_ARTIFACT_DIR:-$(dirname "$2")/artifacts}"; mkdir -p "$_art"
114	    [[ "${BUILD_ARM_ABORT:-0}" == "1" ]] && : > "${ZBUILD_STATE_DIR}/.abort.signal"
115	    if [[ "${BUILD_RC:-0}" == "0" ]]; then
116	        printf '%s' '{"result_contract":2,"verdict":"pass","disposition":"complete","reason":"stub"}' > "$_art/build-result.json"
117	    else
118	        printf '%s' '{"result_contract":2,"verdict":"error","disposition":"broken","reason":"stub failure"}' > "$_art/build-result.json"
119	    fi
120	    return "${BUILD_RC:-0}"
121	}
122	build_cleanup() {
123	    printf 'build:%s\n' "${3:-NOSCOPE}" >> "${RELEASE_MARKER}"
124	    # A hook that never returns — used to prove the dispatch is bounded. It
125	    # records its own pid so SPEC-6 can check it does not outlive the run (#2287).
126	    if [[ "${BLOCK_CLEANUP:-0}" == "1" ]]; then
127	        printf '%s\n' "$BASHPID" >> "${RELEASE_MARKER%/*}/hook.pid"
128	        sleep 120
129	    fi
130	    if [[ "${BLOCK_CLEANUP_IGNORE_TERM:-0}" == "1" ]]; then
131	        # #2333: a child that ignores TERM, under a hook shell that does not.
132	        ( trap '' TERM; printf '%s\n' "$BASHPID" >> "${RELEASE_MARKER%/*}/hook-child.pid"; sleep 120 ) &
133	        wait
134	    fi
135	    return 0
136	}
137	PLUG
138	cat > "$PLUGINS_ROOT/tool/test/plugin.sh" <<'PLUG'
139	test_run() {
140	    local _art; _art="${ZBUILD_ARTIFACT_DIR:-$(dirname "$2")/artifacts}"; mkdir -p "$_art"
141	    printf '%s' '{"result_contract":2,"verdict":"pass","disposition":"complete","reason":"stub"}' > "$_art/test-result.json"
142	    return 0
143	}
144	test_cleanup() { printf 'test:%s\n' "${3:-NOSCOPE}" >> "${RELEASE_MARKER}"; return 0; }
145	PLUG
146	
147	OVERLAY_REPO="$(setup_git_temp_repo release-exit-paths-repo)"
148	install_template_overlay "$OVERLAY_REPO" resume-minimal
149	export ZBUILD_SCOPE_OVERRIDE=1
150	mkdir -p "$HOME/.zbuild"
151	printf '%s' "bootstrap" > "$HOME/.zbuild/scope-override-token"
152	
153	_case_no=0
154	# _prep <name> — fresh state dir + marker for one exit path.
155	_prep() {
156	    _case_no=$((_case_no + 1))
157	    CASE_DIR="$TEST_TEMP_DIR/case-$_case_no-$1"
158	    mkdir -p "$CASE_DIR/state" "$CASE_DIR/events"
159	    export ZBUILD_STATE_DIR="$CASE_DIR/state"
160	    export ZBUILD_EVENTS_DIR="$CASE_DIR/events"
161	    export ZBUILD_EVENTS_JSONL="$CASE_DIR/events/events.jsonl"
162	    export ZBUILD_EVENTS_DB="$CASE_DIR/events/events.db"
163	    export RELEASE_MARKER="$CASE_DIR/release-marker"
164	    export BUILD_STARTED="$CASE_DIR/build-started"
165	    : > "$RELEASE_MARKER"
166	    unset BUILD_RC BUILD_SLEEP BUILD_ARM_ABORT 2>/dev/null || true
167	}
168	
169	# _assert_released <case> <stage>... — EVERY named stage released, purge never.
170	#
171	# #1989: this used to grep the shared marker for any ':release' and pass. Three
172	# stages append to that one file, so one stage releasing masked two that never
173	# did — measured: neutering build_cleanup alone left the suite green, and it
174	# took neutering all three to turn it red. The assertion could only ever detect
175	# a TOTAL failure of the mechanism, never a partial one, which is the shape a
176	# real regression takes (#1748: suites observed alive 15+ min after exit).
177	#
178	# Each case now names the stages whose cleanup must have run. The sets differ
179	# by exit path because a stage only reaches release once it has been dispatched.
180	#
181	# ADR-062 §2: reclamation reads the process group recorded at DISPATCH, not the
182	# completion status map, so a stage killed mid-flight IS reclaimable. SPEC-4 and
183	# SPEC-5 therefore expect `build` as well as `intake` — build had demonstrably
184	# started (it wrote BUILD_STARTED) before the signal landed. Before #2001 both
185	# freed `intake` only, because teardown iterated `.stage_statuses`, which
186	# `_update_stage_status` writes only on complete/failed — i.e. after a stage
187	# returns, which a killed stage never does.
188	_assert_released() {
189	    local _case="$1"; shift
190	    local _marker; _marker="$(cat "$RELEASE_MARKER" 2>/dev/null || true)"
191	    local _stage _missing=""
192	    for _stage in "$@"; do
193	        grep -q "^${_stage}:release$" <<< "$_marker" || _missing="${_missing}${_stage} "
194	    done
195	    if [[ -z "$_missing" ]]; then
196	        assert_pass "[$_case] cleanup dispatched with scope=release for: $*"
197	    else
198	        assert_fail "[$_case] cleanup dispatched with scope=release for: $*" \
199	            "no release from: ${_missing}| marker=$(tr '\n' ' ' <<< "$_marker")"
200	    fi
201	    if grep -q ':purge' <<< "$_marker"; then
202	        assert_fail "[$_case] purge is never reachable from a run" "marker contained purge"
203	    else
204	        assert_pass "[$_case] purge is never reachable from a run"
205	    fi
206	}
207	
208	# ── SPEC-1: success ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
209	print_test_section "SPEC-1: exit path = success (rc 0)"
210	_prep success
211	export BUILD_RC=0
212	set +e
213	( cd "$OVERLAY_REPO" && bash "$RUNNER" --template resume-minimal --goal "release-success" ) \
214	    >"$CASE_DIR/out" 2>&1
215	_rc=$?
216	set -e
217	assert_eq "[SPEC-1] runner exits 0 on the success path" "0" "$_rc"
218	_assert_released "SPEC-1" intake build test
219	
220	# ── SPEC-2: non-zero stage rc ────────────────────────────────────────────────
221	print_test_section "SPEC-2: exit path = non-zero stage rc"
222	_prep nonzero
223	export BUILD_RC=1
224	set +e
225	( cd "$OVERLAY_REPO" && bash "$RUNNER" --template resume-minimal --goal "release-nonzero" ) \
226	    >"$CASE_DIR/out" 2>&1
227	_rc=$?
228	set -e
229	if [[ "$_rc" -ne 0 ]]; then
230	    assert_pass "[SPEC-2] runner exits non-zero when a stage fails"
231	else
232	    assert_fail "[SPEC-2] runner exits non-zero when a stage fails" "rc=0"
233	fi
234	_assert_released "SPEC-2" intake build
235	
236	# ── SPEC-3: SIGINT propagation chain (child rc=130 + abort word) ─────────────
237	print_test_section "SPEC-3: exit path = SIGINT chain (stage rc 130, sentinel armed)"
238	_prep sigint
239	export BUILD_RC=130 BUILD_ARM_ABORT=1
240	set +e
241	( cd "$OVERLAY_REPO" && bash "$RUNNER" --template resume-minimal --goal "release-sigint" ) \
242	    >"$CASE_DIR/out" 2>&1
243	_rc=$?
244	set -e
245	# #1850: the run really took the SIGINT path — exit 1 (not 130) and the abort
246	# named sigint — or this case would only repeat SPEC-2's non-zero rc.
247	assert_eq "[SPEC-3] runner exits 1 on the SIGINT chain (not 130)" "1" "$_rc"
248	assert_eq "[SPEC-3] pipeline.aborted carries reason=sigint" "sigint" \
249	    "$(jq -r 'select(.type=="pipeline.aborted") | .data.reason // empty' "$ZBUILD_EVENTS_JSONL" 2>/dev/null | sort -u | tr -d '\n')"
250	_assert_released "SPEC-3" intake build
251	
252	# ── SPEC-4: external SIGTERM ─────────────────────────────────────────────────
253	print_test_section "SPEC-4: exit path = external SIGTERM"
254	_prep sigterm
255	export BUILD_RC=0 BUILD_SLEEP=1
256	if command -v setsid >/dev/null 2>&1; then
257	    setsid bash -c 'cd "$1" && exec bash "$2" --template resume-minimal --goal "$3"' \
258	        _ "$OVERLAY_REPO" "$RUNNER" "release-sigterm" >"$CASE_DIR/out" 2>&1 &
259	    RUNNER_PID=$!
260	else
261	    set -m
262	    bash -c 'cd "$1" && exec bash "$2" --template resume-minimal --goal "$3"' \
263	        _ "$OVERLAY_REPO" "$RUNNER" "release-sigterm" >"$CASE_DIR/out" 2>&1 &
264	    RUNNER_PID=$!
265	    set +m
266	fi
267	for _ in $(seq 1 300); do [[ -f "$BUILD_STARTED" ]] && break; sleep 0.1; done
268	kill -TERM "$RUNNER_PID" 2>/dev/null || true
269	wait "$RUNNER_PID" 2>/dev/null || true
270	# The EXIT trap dispatches release asynchronously w.r.t. this shell's `wait`
271	# on some platforms; give the marker a bounded moment to appear.
272	for _ in $(seq 1 50); do grep -q ':release' "$RELEASE_MARKER" 2>/dev/null && break; sleep 0.1; done
273	_assert_released "SPEC-4" intake build
274	
275	# ── SPEC-5: external hard kill (what an overrunning `timeout` produces) ──────
276	# ADR-053 §2: assert on an observable event, never a wall-clock budget.
277	#
278	# This case used to run the whole runner under `timeout 6`. Those 6 seconds had
279	# to cover process startup, template resolution AND reaching the build stage —
280	# so the budget was really a bet on host speed. Under the parallel pool (#991,
281	# the tier is parallel by default and the serial-pin list is empty) startup
282	# alone outran it: the runner was killed before any stage dispatched, the marker
283	# came back empty, and the failure read as a cleanup regression that standalone
284	# runs could never reproduce.
285	#
286	# The supervising timeout stays, but only as a runaway guard with a ceiling no
287	# healthy run approaches. The kill that this case actually asserts on is driven
288	# from BUILD_STARTED — the runner is provably inside the build stage — and
289	# escalates TERM→KILL the way `timeout` itself does, which is what separates
290	# this case from SPEC-4's plain SIGTERM.
291	print_test_section "SPEC-5: exit path = external hard kill (timeout-style)"
292	_prep timeout
293	export BUILD_RC=0 BUILD_SLEEP=1
294	_tbin=""
295	if   command -v gtimeout >/dev/null 2>&1; then _tbin=gtimeout
296	elif command -v timeout  >/dev/null 2>&1; then _tbin=timeout
297	fi
298	if [[ -z "$_tbin" ]]; then
299	    SKIP=$((SKIP + 1))
300	    echo -e "  ${YELLOW}SKIP${RESET}: [SPEC-5] external hard kill (no timeout binary available)" >&2
301	else
302	    # #2029: the force-kill grace is DERIVED from the engine's own teardown
303	    # budget, not guessed.
304	    #
305	    # The engine bounds each always-run stage by its template `stage_timeout_s`,
306	    # falling back to ZBUILD_STAGE_TIMEOUT_S (default 30s) only when the template
307	    # sets none (#2287) — so the pin below is a fallback, and this case relies on
308	    # its hooks returning promptly rather than on the bound. Three stages
309	    # release on this path, so an unpinned run is entitled to spend far longer
310	    # tidying up than the 3s literal that used to sit here. When it did, this
311	    # test SIGKILLed the runner mid-teardown and then asserted on the markers
312	    # teardown had not yet written: the marker came back EMPTY, with BOTH stages
313	    # missing rather than one. Under a loaded machine that is exactly what
314	    # happened, intermittently, for as long as this test has existed.
315	    #
316	    # Pin the budget so the worst case is knowable, then clear it with margin.
317	    # The backstop exists so a runner that ignores TERM cannot hang the suite —
318	    # it must never be the thing that stops teardown finishing.
319	    _SPEC5_RELEASE_TIMEOUT=3
320	    _SPEC5_KILL_GRACE=$(( _SPEC5_RELEASE_TIMEOUT * 3 + 6 ))   # 3 stages + margin
321	    set -m
322	    ZBUILD_STAGE_TIMEOUT_S="$_SPEC5_RELEASE_TIMEOUT" \
323	    bash -c 'cd "$1" && exec "$4" 120 bash "$2" --template resume-minimal --goal "$3"' \
324	        _ "$OVERLAY_REPO" "$RUNNER" "release-timeout" "$_tbin" >"$CASE_DIR/out" 2>&1 &
325	    RUNNER_PID=$!
326	    set +m
327	    for _ in $(seq 1 300); do [[ -f "$BUILD_STARTED" ]] && break; sleep 0.1; done
328	    kill -TERM -"$RUNNER_PID" 2>/dev/null || kill -TERM "$RUNNER_PID" 2>/dev/null || true
329	    ( sleep "$_SPEC5_KILL_GRACE"; kill -KILL -"$RUNNER_PID" 2>/dev/null || kill -KILL "$RUNNER_PID" 2>/dev/null || true ) &
330	    _spec5_killer=$!
331	    wait "$RUNNER_PID" 2>/dev/null || true
332	    kill "$_spec5_killer" 2>/dev/null || true
333	    wait "$_spec5_killer" 2>/dev/null || true
334	    for _ in $(seq 1 50); do grep -q ':release' "$RELEASE_MARKER" 2>/dev/null && break; sleep 0.1; done
335	    _assert_released "SPEC-5" intake build
336	fi
337	
338	# ── SPEC-6: a blocking cleanup hook cannot hold the exit open ────────────────
339	# The dispatch runs inside the EXIT trap, so an unbounded hook would turn a
340	# normal exit into a hang — the same class of bug (a process that outlives the
341	# run) that this mechanism exists to prevent.
342	print_test_section "SPEC-6: a cleanup hook that blocks cannot hang the runner"
343	_prep blocking
344	export BUILD_RC=0 BLOCK_CLEANUP=1
345	_t0=$(date +%s)
346	set +e
347	( cd "$OVERLAY_REPO" && bash "$RUNNER" --template resume-minimal --goal "release-blocking" ) \
348	    >"$CASE_DIR/out" 2>&1
349	set -e
350	_elapsed=$(( $(date +%s) - _t0 ))
351	unset BLOCK_CLEANUP
352	# The blocking hook sleeps 120s. The bound is the release stage's own
353	# `stage_timeout_s` (30 in the template, which takes precedence over
354	# ZBUILD_STAGE_TIMEOUT_S), so the runner returns in about 30s. Allow generous
355	# headroom for a loaded host while still failing an unbounded wait.
356	if [[ "$_elapsed" -lt 60 ]]; then
357	    assert_pass "[SPEC-6] blocking cleanup is bounded (runner exited in ${_elapsed}s)"
358	else
359	    assert_fail "[SPEC-6] blocking cleanup is bounded" "runner took ${_elapsed}s"
360	fi
361	# #2287: the bound must stop the hook, not just stop waiting for it. Before,
362	# the hook lived on after the run, finished its sleep ~2 min later, and wrote
363	# into a state folder the run no longer owned. The kills are sent before the
364	# runner returns; the 1s grace only covers the killed processes exiting on a
365	# loaded host.
366	sleep 1
367	_hook_pid="$(head -n 1 "$CASE_DIR/hook.pid" 2>/dev/null || true)"
368	if [[ -z "$_hook_pid" ]]; then
369	    assert_fail "[SPEC-6] fixture: the blocking hook recorded its pid" "no $CASE_DIR/hook.pid"
370	elif kill -0 "$_hook_pid" 2>/dev/null; then
371	    assert_fail "[SPEC-6] the blocked hook does not outlive the run" "pid $_hook_pid still alive after the runner returned"
372	    # Leave nothing behind for the rest of the suite: the hook first, so it
373	    # cannot carry on once its sleep ends, then the sleep it leaves orphaned.
374	    _hook_kids="$(pgrep -P "$_hook_pid" 2>/dev/null || true)"
375	    kill -KILL "$_hook_pid" 2>/dev/null || true
376	    for _k in $_hook_kids; do kill -KILL "$_k" 2>/dev/null || true; done
377	else
378	    assert_pass "[SPEC-6] the blocked hook does not outlive the run"
379	fi
380	
381	# ── SPEC-6b (#2333): a child that ignores TERM is killed too ────────────────
382	# The bound sends TERM to the hook's group, then KILL after a grace. The runner
383	# waited only for the group leader and cancelled the watchdog when it exited, so
384	# a member that ignored TERM never got the KILL and outlived the run.
385	print_test_section "SPEC-6b: a hook child that ignores TERM does not outlive the run"
386	# The time bound itself is SPEC-6's check, on the same dispatch path; this
387	# case is only about what survives it.
388	_prep blocking-ignore-term
389	export BUILD_RC=0 BLOCK_CLEANUP_IGNORE_TERM=1
390	set +e
391	( cd "$OVERLAY_REPO" && bash "$RUNNER" --template resume-minimal --goal "release-ignore-term" ) \
392	    >"$CASE_DIR/out" 2>&1
393	set -e
394	unset BLOCK_CLEANUP_IGNORE_TERM
395	_child_pid=""
396	for _ in $(seq 1 50); do
397	    _child_pid="$(head -n 1 "$CASE_DIR/hook-child.pid" 2>/dev/null || true)"
398	    [[ -n "$_child_pid" ]] && break; sleep 0.1
399	done
400	_alive=1
401	# Only poll a pid that was recorded; a missing pid is reported as a fixture failure below.
402	if [[ -n "$_child_pid" ]]; then
403	    for _ in $(seq 1 50); do kill -0 "$_child_pid" 2>/dev/null || { _alive=0; break; }; sleep 0.1; done
404	fi
405	if [[ -z "$_child_pid" ]]; then
406	    assert_fail "[SPEC-6b] fixture: the child recorded its pid" "no $CASE_DIR/hook-child.pid"
407	elif [[ "$_alive" -eq 1 ]]; then
408	    assert_fail "[SPEC-6b] a hook child that ignores TERM does not outlive the run" "pid $_child_pid still alive 5s after the runner returned"
409	    kill -KILL "$_child_pid" 2>/dev/null || true
410	else
411	    assert_pass "[SPEC-6b] a hook child that ignores TERM does not outlive the run"
412	fi
413	
414	# ── SPEC-2ext [#1801/SPEC-2]: external SIGTERM kills the run hook's process group
415	# SPEC-2 says: "when the runner is externally killed, its signal handler must
416	# also kill any isolated hook process group". The run hook spawns a child that
417	# ignores TERM. After the runner is externally killed, the child must not survive
418	# because zbuild_pg_kill (or the equivalent KILL sequence) sends SIGKILL to the
419	# entire process group, which the child cannot ignore.
420	print_test_section "SPEC-2ext: external SIGTERM kills the run hook's process group [#1801/SPEC-2]"
421	_prep sigterm-runpg
422	export BUILD_RC=0 BUILD_RUN_SPAWN_IGNORE_TERM=1
423	if command -v setsid >/dev/null 2>&1; then
424	    setsid bash -c 'cd "$1" && exec bash "$2" --template resume-minimal --goal "$3"' \
425	        _ "$OVERLAY_REPO" "$RUNNER" "release-sigterm-runpg" >"$CASE_DIR/out" 2>&1 &
426	    RUNNER_PID=$!
427	else
428	    set -m
429	    bash -c 'cd "$1" && exec bash "$2" --template resume-minimal --goal "$3"' \
430	        _ "$OVERLAY_REPO" "$RUNNER" "release-sigterm-runpg" >"$CASE_DIR/out" 2>&1 &
431	    RUNNER_PID=$!
432	    set +m
433	fi
434	_run_child_pid=""
435	for _ in $(seq 1 100); do
436	    _run_child_pid="$(head -n 1 "$CASE_DIR/run-child.pid" 2>/dev/null || true)"
437	    [[ -n "$_run_child_pid" ]] && break; sleep 0.1
438	done
439	kill -TERM "$RUNNER_PID" 2>/dev/null || true
440	wait "$RUNNER_PID" 2>/dev/null || true
441	unset BUILD_RUN_SPAWN_IGNORE_TERM
442	_alive_run=1
443	if [[ -n "$_run_child_pid" ]]; then
444	    for _ in $(seq 1 50); do kill -0 "$_run_child_pid" 2>/dev/null || { _alive_run=0; break; }; sleep 0.1; done
445	fi
446	if [[ -z "$_run_child_pid" ]]; then
447	    assert_fail "[#1801/SPEC-2] fixture: run hook child recorded its pid" "no $CASE_DIR/run-child.pid"
448	elif [[ "$_alive_run" -eq 1 ]]; then
449	    assert_fail "[#1801/SPEC-2] external SIGTERM: run hook process group is killed (TERM-ignoring child gone)" \
450	        "pid $_run_child_pid still alive — hook process group was not killed when runner received SIGTERM"
451	    kill -KILL "$_run_child_pid" 2>/dev/null || true
452	else
453	    assert_pass "[#1801/SPEC-2] external SIGTERM: run hook process group is killed (TERM-ignoring child gone)"
454	fi
455	
456	cleanup_test_env
457	print_test_results
458	exit $((FAIL > 0))

1	#!/usr/bin/env bash
2	# Integration test (Wave 15-H / #688): flag-gated process-group signal
3	# forwarding via bash job control in the runner.
4	#
5	# When ZBUILD_RUNNER_JOB_CONTROL=1:
6	#   - the runner enables `set -m` at startup;
7	#   - the SIGINT/TERM trap walks `jobs -p` and TERM-then-KILL's each
8	#     child PGID, reaping whole subtrees.
9	#
10	# Discriminating assertions:
11	#   (T1) With flag on, the runner shell has `monitor` (-m) option set —
12	#        verified by injecting a probe plugin that records `$-` and
13	#        `set -o monitor` output. Flag-off: no `-m`.
14	#   (T2) With flag on, SIGTERM mid-build still produces exit 1 + the
15	#        Wave 15-B sentinel/event chain (regression of trap composition) —
16	#        the signal is named by pipeline.aborted reason=sigterm (#1850,
17	#        ADR-054 §4: the exit status was 143).
18	#
19	# Wave 15-H lays the foundation for future backgrounded stages (e.g.
20	# parallel strategy fanout); the trap's PG-kill loop is exercised here
21	# transitively by T2's end-to-end SIGTERM. The current dispatch path
22	# runs plugins in foreground subshells (no `&`), so a flag-on test that
23	# requires a backgrounded runner-child would not reflect realistic usage
24	# and is intentionally omitted.
25	#
26	set -euo pipefail
27	
28	SCRIPT_DIR="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)"
29	REPO_ROOT="$(cd "$SCRIPT_DIR/../.." && pwd)"
30	RUNNER="$REPO_ROOT/core/pipeline/runner.sh"
31	
32	# shellcheck source=../../scripts/lib/helpers.sh
33	source "$REPO_ROOT/scripts/lib/helpers.sh"
34	# shellcheck source=../../scripts/lib/test-helpers.sh
35	source "$REPO_ROOT/scripts/lib/test-helpers.sh"
36	
37	print_test_header "runner job-control PG forwarding (Wave 15-H / #688)"
38	setup_test_env "runner-job-control-abort"
39	
40	_test_cleanup_hook() {
41	    if [[ "${KEEP_TMP:-0}" == "1" ]]; then
42	        echo "KEEPTEMP=$TEST_TEMP_DIR" >&2
43	    else
44	        cleanup_test_env
45	    fi
46	}
47	
48	export ZBUILD_CONTRACT_VALIDATOR=warn
49	export ZBUILD_SCOPE_OVERRIDE=1
50	mkdir -p "$HOME/.zbuild"
51	printf '%s' "bootstrap" > "$HOME/.zbuild/scope-override-token"
52	
53	# ─── T1: flag toggles `-m` (monitor mode) on the runner shell ────────────────
54	print_test_section "T1: ZBUILD_RUNNER_JOB_CONTROL=1 enables set -m in runner"
55	
56	PROBE_STATE_DIR="$TEST_TEMP_DIR/state-probe"
57	PROBE_PLUGINS="$TEST_TEMP_DIR/plugins"   # mock_plugin_factory uses TEST_TEMP_DIR/plugins
58	PROBE_EVENTS="$TEST_TEMP_DIR/events-probe/events.jsonl"
59	mkdir -p "$PROBE_STATE_DIR" "$TEST_TEMP_DIR/events-probe"
60	PROBE_OPTS_FILE="$TEST_TEMP_DIR/intake-shell-opts"
61	
62	export ZBUILD_PLUGINS_ROOT="$PROBE_PLUGINS"
63	export ZBUILD_STATE_DIR="$PROBE_STATE_DIR"
64	export ZBUILD_EVENTS_DIR="$TEST_TEMP_DIR/events-probe"
65	export ZBUILD_EVENTS_JSONL="$PROBE_EVENTS"
66	export ZBUILD_EVENT_SCHEMA="$REPO_ROOT/config/event-schema.json"
67	export ZBUILD_MODELS_FILE="$REPO_ROOT/config/models.json"
68	export ZBUILD_CYCLES_ENABLED=0
69	
70	# #978: job-control PG forwarding is roster-agnostic — T1 probes the runner
71	# shell's monitor-mode via intake, and T2 signals mid-build and asserts test
72	# never runs. Drive a MINIMAL 3-leaf fixture (intake → build → test) instead of
73	# pinning to the standard roster (retired in #979). #1270: install the fixture as
74	# a per-repo `.zbuild/templates/` overlay in a temp repo and run with CWD = that
75	# repo (the resolver reads the overlay from $PWD). intake/build/test get custom
76	# bodies below.
77	OVERLAY_REPO="$(setup_git_temp_repo tpl-overlay-repo)"
78	install_template_overlay "$OVERLAY_REPO" resume-minimal
79	mock_plugin_factory "intake" "agent" 0 >/dev/null
80	mock_plugin_factory "build"  "agent" 0 >/dev/null
81	mock_plugin_factory "test"   "tool"  0 >/dev/null
82	
83	# Probe intake records $- (set of shell option flags) to a marker so we
84	# can introspect whether the runner shell has 'm' (monitor mode) set.
85	cat > "$PROBE_PLUGINS/agent/intake/plugin.sh" <<PROBE
86	intake_run() {
87	    echo "dash=\$-" > "${PROBE_OPTS_FILE}"
88	    set -o | grep -E '^monitor' >> "${PROBE_OPTS_FILE}" 2>/dev/null || true
89	    $(mock_v2_result_line intake)
90	    return 0
91	}
92	PROBE
93	
94	# Run with flag OFF.
95	: > "$PROBE_OPTS_FILE"
96	unset ZBUILD_RUNNER_JOB_CONTROL
97	rm -f "$PROBE_STATE_DIR/pipeline-state.json"
98	set +e
99	# #1270: CWD = overlay repo so the resolver finds the resume-minimal fixture.
100	( cd "$OVERLAY_REPO" && bash "$RUNNER" --template resume-minimal --goal "w15h probe flag-off" ) \
101	    >"$TEST_TEMP_DIR/runner-off.stdout" 2>"$TEST_TEMP_DIR/runner-off.stderr"
102	rc_off=$?
103	set -e
104	opts_off="$(cat "$PROBE_OPTS_FILE" 2>/dev/null || echo "")"
105	
106	# Run with flag ON.
107	: > "$PROBE_OPTS_FILE"
108	export ZBUILD_RUNNER_JOB_CONTROL=1
109	rm -f "$PROBE_STATE_DIR/pipeline-state.json"
110	set +e
111	( cd "$OVERLAY_REPO" && bash "$RUNNER" --template resume-minimal --goal "w15h probe flag-on" ) \
112	    >"$TEST_TEMP_DIR/runner-on.stdout" 2>"$TEST_TEMP_DIR/runner-on.stderr"
113	rc_on=$?
114	set -e
115	opts_on="$(cat "$PROBE_OPTS_FILE" 2>/dev/null || echo "")"
116	
117	# Both runs must exit 0.
118	assert_eq "flag-off probe run rc=0" "0" "$rc_off"
119	assert_eq "flag-on  probe run rc=0" "0" "$rc_on"
120	# #2193: a probe that exits non-zero must say why — CI showed only "got: 1".
121	for _pr in off on; do
122	    _rcv="rc_$_pr"
123	    if [[ "${!_rcv}" != "0" ]]; then
124	        echo "--- runner-$_pr.stderr (tail) ---" >&2
125	        tail -30 "$TEST_TEMP_DIR/runner-$_pr.stderr" >&2 2>/dev/null || true
126	    fi
127	done
128	
129	# Flag-off: $- must NOT contain 'm'; set -o monitor must be off.
130	if grep -qE 'dash=[^m]*$|dash=[^m]*[^m]*$' <<< "$opts_off" && \
131	   grep -qE '^monitor[[:space:]]+off$' <<< "$opts_off"; then
132	    assert_pass "flag-off: monitor mode OFF in runner shell"
133	else
134	    # Looser check: dash line should not have 'm'.
135	    _opts_off_1="$(head -1 <<< "$opts_off")"
136	    if grep -qv 'm' <<< "$_opts_off_1"; then
137	        assert_pass "flag-off: monitor mode OFF in runner shell (dash check)"
138	    else
139	        assert_fail "flag-off: monitor mode OFF in runner shell" \
140	            "got: $opts_off"
141	    fi
142	fi
143	
144	# Flag-on: $- must contain 'm' OR set -o monitor must be on.
145	_opts_on_1="$(head -1 <<< "$opts_on")"
146	if grep -q 'm' <<< "$_opts_on_1" || \
147	   grep -qE '^monitor[[:space:]]+on$' <<< "$opts_on"; then
148	    assert_pass "flag-on: monitor mode ON in runner shell"
149	else
150	    assert_fail "flag-on: monitor mode ON in runner shell" \
151	        "got: $opts_on"
152	fi
153	
154	# ─── T2: SIGTERM with flag-on still produces exit 1 + Wave 15-B chain ────────
155	print_test_section "T2: end-to-end SIGTERM with flag-on (regression of trap chain)"
156	
157	# Reuse $PROBE_PLUGINS (= TEST_TEMP_DIR/plugins). Override build/test/intake.
158	E2E_STATE_DIR="$TEST_TEMP_DIR/state-e2e"
159	E2E_EVENTS_JSONL="$TEST_TEMP_DIR/events-e2e/events.jsonl"
160	export ZBUILD_STATE_DIR="$E2E_STATE_DIR"
161	export ZBUILD_EVENTS_DIR="$TEST_TEMP_DIR/events-e2e"
162	export ZBUILD_EVENTS_JSONL="$E2E_EVENTS_JSONL"
163	mkdir -p "$E2E_STATE_DIR" "$TEST_TEMP_DIR/events-e2e"
164	export ZBUILD_RUNNER_JOB_CONTROL=1
165	
166	E2E_BUILD_STARTED="$TEST_TEMP_DIR/e2e-build-started"
167	E2E_TEST_RAN="$TEST_TEMP_DIR/e2e-test-ran"
168	export E2E_BUILD_STARTED E2E_TEST_RAN
169	
170	# Restore intake to a no-op (was overridden by probe).
171	cat > "$PROBE_PLUGINS/agent/intake/plugin.sh" <<PLUG
172	intake_run() { $(mock_v2_result_line intake); return 0; }
173	PLUG
174	
175	# Build plugin: short polling loop so the trap can fire within budget.
176	# Note: under flag-on, `set -m` puts the plugin subshell in its own PGID
177	# so a kernel-pgrp TERM to the runner does NOT reach the subshell directly.
178	# The runner's trap therefore fires only after the foreground subshell
179	# returns naturally — bounded by the loop length here.
180	cat > "$PROBE_PLUGINS/agent/build/plugin.sh" <<PLUG
181	build_run() {
182	    : > "${E2E_BUILD_STARTED}"
183	    local _i
184	    for _i in \$(seq 1 30); do
185	        sleep 0.1
186	    done
187	    $(mock_v2_result_line build)
188	    return 0
189	}
190	PLUG
191	cat > "$PROBE_PLUGINS/tool/test/plugin.sh" <<PLUG
192	test_run() { : > "${E2E_TEST_RAN}"; $(mock_v2_result_line test); return 0; }
193	PLUG
194	
195	# #1270: the runner resolves the fixture from $PWD, so cd into the overlay repo
196	# before exec-ing it. `exec` replaces the wrapper shell so $! is the runner PID.
197	if command -v setsid >/dev/null 2>&1; then
198	    setsid bash -c 'cd "$1" && exec bash "$2" --template resume-minimal --goal "$3"' \
199	        _ "$OVERLAY_REPO" "$RUNNER" "w15h e2e" \

Here are the full contents of all six files:

---

**1. `tests/unit/stage-timeout-dispatch-test.sh`** (191 lines)

Tests `[#1801/SPEC-1]` and `[#1801/SPEC-10]`. Verifies that `plugin_hook_call` in `core/plugin-registry/lifecycle.sh` contains a per-dispatch timeout watchdog guarded to the `run` hook, that the watchdog writes a `timed_out` disposition (with `stage=` and `timeout_s=` fields in the `plugin.run.timed_out` event), that all dispatch routes (fanout.sh, sequential.sh, map.sh, runner.sh) reach `plugin_hook_call`, that no hand-rolled `kill -TERM`/`kill -KILL` remains in `plugin_hook_call`, that `_orch_local_collect_results` uses `zbuild_pg_kill`/`zbuild_pid_kill`, that `_orch_local_kill_slot` is removed, and that orch-ruflo-hive carries no suppressing TERM/KILL sequence.

---

**2. `tests/unit/stage-timeout-no-flat-limit-test.sh`** (63 lines)

Tests `[#1801/SPEC-7]`. Source-level assertions that none of the three strategy files (`fanout.sh`, `sequential.sh`, `map.sh`) reference `ZBUILD_ORCH_TIMEOUT`, and that no `orch_collect`/`orch_wait` call carries a `--timeout` flag. Ensures the per-dispatch watchdog in lifecycle.sh is the only stage time limit.

---

**3. `tests/unit/stage-timeout-precedence-test.sh`** (155 lines)

Tests `[#1801/SPEC-3]`. Sources `core/pipeline/template.sh` and verifies three precedence tiers: (1) `stage_timeout_s` in the template beats `ZBUILD_STAGE_TIMEOUT_S` env var (expects `_TPL_STAGE_TIMEOUT_S_alpha=7200`), (2) `ZBUILD_STAGE_TIMEOUT_S` beats the 5400 s engine default (template var must be unset or equal to env value), and (3) `5400` appears as the terminal fallback inside `plugin_hook_call`. Also verifies `load_template` exports `_TPL_STAGE_TIMEOUT_S_<stage>` from the YAML field.

---

**4. `tests/unit/orch-backend-misconfigured-test.sh`** (146 lines)

Tests `[#1801/SPEC-9]`. Verifies that `orch_load_backend` in `core/orch/contract.sh` fails with a `misconfigured` message naming the backend (not silent fallback) for: an unknown alias, a missing-plugins-root scenario (non-zero exit required), and an unreadable `manifest.yaml` (chmod 000). Also asserts the old `orch-sequential` fallback reference is removed from `contract.sh`.

---

**5. `tests/integration/runner-release-exit-paths-test.sh`** (459 lines)

Integration test for `#1829` / ADR-054 §7. Uses a 3-plugin fixture (intake, build, test) with a `resume-minimal` template overlay. Asserts cleanup with scope `release` (never `purge`) fires on every exit path: SPEC-1 (success), SPEC-2 (non-zero stage rc), SPEC-3 (SIGINT chain, rc=130 + abort sentinel), SPEC-4 (external SIGTERM), SPEC-5 (external hard kill / timeout-style), SPEC-6 (blocking cleanup hook is bounded, hook does not outlive the run — #2287), SPEC-6b (hook child that ignores TERM is killed too — #2333), and SPEC-2ext (`[#1801/SPEC-2]`: external SIGTERM kills the run hook's entire process group including TERM-ignoring children via `zbuild_pg_kill`).

---

**6. `tests/integration/runner-job-control-abort-test.sh`** (282 lines)

Integration test for Wave 15-H / #688. Tests `ZBUILD_RUNNER_JOB_CONTROL=1` flag behavior. T1: verifies the runner shell has monitor mode (`set -m`) when flag is on and not when flag is off, by injecting a probe plugin that records `$-` and `set -o monitor` output. T2: end-to-end SIGTERM with flag-on verifies exit code is `1` (not `143`), `pipeline.aborted` event carries `reason=sigterm`, the test stage did not run, `pipeline-state.json` shows `status=interrupted`, and no job-control errors appear in stderr.

content.text:
Here are the full contents of all six files:

---

**1. `tests/unit/stage-timeout-dispatch-test.sh`** (191 lines)

Tests `[#1801/SPEC-1]` and `[#1801/SPEC-10]`. Verifies that `plugin_hook_call` in `core/plugin-registry/lifecycle.sh` contains a per-dispatch timeout watchdog guarded to the `run` hook, that the watchdog writes a `timed_out` disposition (with `stage=` and `timeout_s=` fields in the `plugin.run.timed_out` event), that all dispatch routes (fanout.sh, sequential.sh, map.sh, runner.sh) reach `plugin_hook_call`, that no hand-rolled `kill -TERM`/`kill -KILL` remains in `plugin_hook_call`, that `_orch_local_collect_results` uses `zbuild_pg_kill`/`zbuild_pid_kill`, that `_orch_local_kill_slot` is removed, and that orch-ruflo-hive carries no suppressing TERM/KILL sequence.

---

**2. `tests/unit/stage-timeout-no-flat-limit-test.sh`** (63 lines)

Tests `[#1801/SPEC-7]`. Source-level assertions that none of the three strategy files (`fanout.sh`, `sequential.sh`, `map.sh`) reference `ZBUILD_ORCH_TIMEOUT`, and that no `orch_collect`/`orch_wait` call carries a `--timeout` flag. Ensures the per-dispatch watchdog in lifecycle.sh is the only stage time limit.

---

**3. `tests/unit/stage-timeout-precedence-test.sh`** (155 lines)

Tests `[#1801/SPEC-3]`. Sources `core/pipeline/template.sh` and verifies three precedence tiers: (1) `stage_timeout_s` in the template beats `ZBUILD_STAGE_TIMEOUT_S` env var (expects `_TPL_STAGE_TIMEOUT_S_alpha=7200`), (2) `ZBUILD_STAGE_TIMEOUT_S` beats the 5400 s engine default (template var must be unset or equal to env value), and (3) `5400` appears as the terminal fallback inside `plugin_hook_call`. Also verifies `load_template` exports `_TPL_STAGE_TIMEOUT_S_<stage>` from the YAML field.

---

**4. `tests/unit/orch-backend-misconfigured-test.sh`** (146 lines)

Tests `[#1801/SPEC-9]`. Verifies that `orch_load_backend` in `core/orch/contract.sh` fails with a `misconfigured` message naming the backend (not silent fallback) for: an unknown alias, a missing-plugins-root scenario (non-zero exit required), and an unreadable `manifest.yaml` (chmod 000). Also asserts the old `orch-sequential` fallback reference is removed from `contract.sh`.

---

**5. `tests/integration/runner-release-exit-paths-test.sh`** (459 lines)

Integration test for `#1829` / ADR-054 §7. Uses a 3-plugin fixture (intake, build, test) with a `resume-minimal` template overlay. Asserts cleanup with scope `release` (never `purge`) fires on every exit path: SPEC-1 (success), SPEC-2 (non-zero stage rc), SPEC-3 (SIGINT chain, rc=130 + abort sentinel), SPEC-4 (external SIGTERM), SPEC-5 (external hard kill / timeout-style), SPEC-6 (blocking cleanup hook is bounded, hook does not outlive the run — #2287), SPEC-6b (hook child that ignores TERM is killed too — #2333), and SPEC-2ext (`[#1801/SPEC-2]`: external SIGTERM kills the run hook's entire process group including TERM-ignoring children via `zbuild_pg_kill`).

---

**6. `tests/integration/runner-job-control-abort-test.sh`** (282 lines)

Integration test for Wave 15-H / #688. Tests `ZBUILD_RUNNER_JOB_CONTROL=1` flag behavior. T1: verifies the runner shell has monitor mode (`set -m`) when flag is on and not when flag is off, by injecting a probe plugin that records `$-` and `set -o monitor` output. T2: end-to-end SIGTERM with flag-on verifies exit code is `1` (not `143`), `pipeline.aborted` event carries `reason=sigterm`, the test stage did not run, `pipeline-state.json` shows `status=interrupted`, and no job-control errors appear in stderr.

41	  gate: auto
42	  roles: [intake]
43	  stage_timeout_s: 30
44	  router:
45	    timeout_s: 600
46	  io:
47	    destinations: [file]
48	'

66	  io:

2	# [#1801/SPEC-8] Guard: orch-sequential is retired.
3	#
4	# After this change:
5	#   - plugins/tool/orch-sequential/ does not exist on disk
6	#   - no file outside docs/adr/ names "orch-sequential"
7	#   - configuring `sequential` as an orchestrator backend makes the run end as
8	#     `misconfigured`
9	#
10	# [#1801/SPEC-11] Guard: ADR-054 §9, ADR-017, and ADR-011 have ## Enforced by
11	# sections and are NOT in config/adr-enforcement-baseline.txt.
12	#
13	# These tests FAIL on pre-change code (where orch-sequential still exists, where
14	# code files still reference it, and where the ADRs lack Enforced-by sections)
15	# and PASS after the change.
16	set -euo pipefail
17	
18	SCRIPT_DIR="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)"
19	REPO_ROOT="$(cd "$SCRIPT_DIR/../.." && pwd)"
20

23	# shellcheck source=../../scripts/lib/test-helpers.sh
24	source "$REPO_ROOT/scripts/lib/test-helpers.sh"
25	
26	print_test_header "[#1801/SPEC-8] orch-sequential retired; [#1801/SPEC-11] ADR Enforced-by sections"
27

29	print_test_section "[#1801/SPEC-8] plugins/tool/orch-sequential/ is absent"
30	
31	if [[ -e "$REPO_ROOT/plugins/tool/orch-sequential" ]]; then
32	    assert_fail "[#1801/SPEC-8] plugins/tool/orch-sequential/ is absent" \
33	        "directory still exists — the retired backend was not removed"
34	else

36	fi
37

39	print_test_section "[#1801/SPEC-8] no file outside docs/adr/ names orch-sequential"
40	
41	# Directories the guard allows: docs/adr/ (historical references are fine there)
42	# and tests/golden (the golden for the deleted plugin will also be gone).
43	# The guard runs via grep -r, excluding those two directories.
44	_bad_refs=""
45	while IFS= read -r _match; do
46	    [[ -z "$_match" ]] && continue
47	    # Strip repo root prefix for readability
48	    _rel="${_match#$REPO_ROOT/}"
49	    _bad_refs+="  $_rel"$'\n'
50	done < <(grep -rl 'orch-sequential' "$REPO_ROOT" \
51	    --exclude-dir='.git' \
52	    --exclude-dir='legacy-DoNotUse' 2>/dev/null | \
53	    grep -v '^'"$REPO_ROOT"'/docs/adr/' | \
54	    grep -v '^'"$REPO_ROOT"'/tests/golden/' | \
55	    grep -v '^'"$REPO_ROOT"'/tests/unit/orch-sequential-retired-guard-test\.sh$' | \
56	    grep -v '^'"$REPO_ROOT"'/tests/unit/orch-backend-misconfigured-test\.sh$' || true)
57	
58	if [[ -n "$_bad_refs" ]]; then
59	    assert_fail "[#1801/SPEC-8] no file outside docs/adr/ names orch-sequential" \
60	        "found references:"$'\n'"$_bad_refs"
61	else
62	    assert_pass "[#1801/SPEC-8] no file outside docs/adr/ names orch-sequential"
63	fi
64	
65	# ─── [#1801/SPEC-8] configuring sequential as backend → misconfigured ─────────
66	print_test_section "[#1801/SPEC-8] configuring sequential as a backend ends the run as misconfigured"
67	
68	# source contract.sh with a controlled env so _orch_load_backend uses the
69	# sequential alias and we can capture its outcome.
70	_orch_result=""
71	_orch_rc=0
72	_orch_result="$(
73	    ZBUILD_ORCH_BACKEND=sequential \
74	    ZBUILD_PLUGINS_ROOT="$REPO_ROOT/plugins" \
75	    bash -c '

77	        source "'"$REPO_ROOT"'/core/orch/contract.sh" 2>/dev/null || true
78	        # After the change, orch_load_backend emits orch.backend.misconfigured
79	        # or writes a misconfigured disposition; check what the function does.
80	        orch_load_backend sequential 2>&1
81	        echo "rc=$?"
82	    ' 2>&1)" || _orch_rc=$?
83	
84	# The requirement: configuring sequential emits misconfigured
85	# Accept either an event name match or an explicit "misconfigured" in output
86	if grep -qiE 'misconfigured|sequential.*not found|backend.*sequential.*not' <<< "$_orch_result"; then
87	    assert_pass "[#1801/SPEC-8] configuring sequential as backend signals misconfigured"
88	else
89	    assert_fail "[#1801/SPEC-8] configuring sequential as backend signals misconfigured" \
90	        "output: $(printf '%s' "$_orch_result" | head -5 | tr '\n' '|')"
91	fi
92	
93	# ─── [#1801/SPEC-11] ADR-054 has ## Enforced by section ──────────────────────
94	print_test_section "[#1801/SPEC-11] ADR-054 has ## Enforced by section"
95

99	else

101	        assert_pass "[#1801/SPEC-11] ADR-054 has ## Enforced by section"
102	    else
103	        assert_fail "[#1801/SPEC-11] ADR-054 has ## Enforced by section" \
104	            "section absent — ADR-054 §9 requires it"
105	    fi
106	fi
107

109	print_test_section "[#1801/SPEC-11] ADR-017 has ## Enforced by section"
110	
111	_adr017="$REPO_ROOT/docs/adr/ADR-017-per-stage-router-config.md"
112	if [[ ! -f "$_adr017" ]]; then
113	    assert_fail "[#1801/SPEC-11] ADR-017 exists" "file not found: $_adr017"
114	else
115	    if grep -qE '^## Enforced by' "$_adr017"; then
116	        assert_pass "[#1801/SPEC-11] ADR-017 has ## Enforced by section"
117	    else
118	        assert_fail "[#1801/SPEC-11] ADR-017 has ## Enforced by section" \
119	            "section absent"
120	    fi
121	fi
122	
123	# ─── [#1801/SPEC-11] ADR-011 has ## Enforced by section ──────────────────────
124	print_test_section "[#1801/SPEC-11] ADR-011 has ## Enforced by section"
125	
126	_adr011="$REPO_ROOT/docs/adr/ADR-011-pluggable-backends.md"
127	if [[ ! -f "$_adr011" ]]; then
128	    assert_fail "[#1801/SPEC-11] ADR-011 exists" "file not found: $_adr011"
129	else
130	    if grep -qE '^## Enforced by' "$_adr011"; then
131	        assert_pass "[#1801/SPEC-11] ADR-011 has ## Enforced by section"
132	    else
133	        assert_fail "[#1801/SPEC-11] ADR-011 has ## Enforced by section" \
134	            "section absent"
135	    fi
136	fi
137	
138	# ─── [#1801/SPEC-11] the three ADRs are not in the enforcement baseline ───────
139	print_test_section "[#1801/SPEC-11] ADR-054, ADR-017, ADR-011 removed from adr-enforcement-baseline.txt"
140	
141	_baseline="$REPO_ROOT/config/adr-enforcement-baseline.txt"
142	if [[ ! -f "$_baseline" ]]; then
143	    assert_fail "[#1801/SPEC-11] config/adr-enforcement-baseline.txt exists" \
144	        "file not found: $_baseline"
145	else
146	    for _adr_name in ADR-054 ADR-017 ADR-011; do
147	        if grep -q "$_adr_name" "$_baseline"; then
148	            assert_fail "[#1801/SPEC-11] $_adr_name is not in adr-enforcement-baseline.txt" \
149	                "$_adr_name still listed — remove after adding its Enforced-by section"
150	        else
151	            assert_pass "[#1801/SPEC-11] $_adr_name is not in adr-enforcement-baseline.txt"
152	        fi

440	rc says whether a stage *ran*; the verdict says how it *went*. A cycle already acts on its members' verdicts. A leaf stage — one outside any cycle or map: `hydrate`, `intake`, `plan`, `review-aggregator`, `pr`, and `deployed.yaml`'s `deploy`, `validate`, `monitor` — did not: the runner read its verdict, recorded it, picked a glyph from it, and marked the stage `complete`, so a run whose intake, plan or pr reported `fail` with rc 0 ended `success` and opened a pull request. #2231 closed the rejected-result case (a contract violation); this closes the well-formed result that says it failed.
441	
442	- A leaf whose verdict is fail-class (`fail`, `error`, `block`, `scope_violation`, `corrupt_diff`) ends the run on both paths a leaf finishes on (the dispatch-unit loop and the linear loop): the stage is `failed`, the run ends `failed` with `reason=stage_failed:<the stage's word>`, and no later stage runs.
443	- A template marks a leaf advisory with `blocking: false` (ADR-013's attribute, now recorded when false as well as true); its failing verdict is recorded and the run goes on. `deployed.yaml` marks `monitor` so, as ADR-013's table lists it.
444	- pass- and warn-class verdicts (`pass`, `complete`, `degraded`, …) complete as before.
445	
446	Verification: `tests/integration/leaf-verdict-halts-test.sh` (SPEC-1–4, both loops), `tests/unit/template-blocking-reset-test.sh` SPEC-5/6, `tests/unit/run-open-items-test.sh` O3 (the end in words).
447	
448	### Amendment (2026-10-08, #1850) — §4/§5: one contract, and rc is binary everywhere
449	
450	§4b's end state, delivered. Versioned coexistence is over, and the engine's own paths hold the rule §4 states for stages.
451	
452	**The result contract (§4b, §5).**
453	- `result_contract: 2` is the only version the engine accepts (`_ZBUILD_CONTRACT_MIN=2`, the single declaration in `core/contract/version.sh`). A stage plugin that declares 1, or none, is refused at load with a message naming the plugin and the accepted range. A plugin with no primary output (a persona, a backend) is not a stage and is not asked.
454	- The v1 reader, the `<stage>-verdict.json` sidecar as a verdict source, and the legacy rc mapping (`dispatch_rc_legacy_reason`) are deleted, not bypassed.
455	- Every lenient no-result default is a structural failure: no manifest, no primary declared, a non-JSON primary, a JSON primary with no `.verdict`, and an absent result (`contract_violation:*`). A leaf that exits 0 having written nothing ends the run.
456	
457	**rc is binary on the engine's own paths (§4, §4a).** Every signal §4a lists now travels on its declared channel and nothing returns or reads the number:
458	- A loop (`cycle_orchestrator_run`) returns 0 when it converged, else 1, and says how it ended in words — `_CYCLE_LAST_OUTCOME` (`converged`, `unconverged`, `interrupted`, `failed`, `aborted`) and `_CYCLE_LAST_TERMINATED_REASON`. The runner acts on the outcome. A nested `cycle_abort` reaches the operator as `cycle_abort`, never as `config_invalid` (#1860).
459	- An abort — Ctrl-C, a kill, an `abort_when` match, an unavailable or rate-limited model, an oversized scope — is a word recorded once on ADR-025's channel. The run ends on that word: `interrupted` or `aborted`, with `pipeline.aborted reason=<word>`. The runner process exits 1.
460	- A parallel group returns 0/1. A dispatch strategy returns 0/1 and names why on `_ZB_STRATEGY_OUTCOME`. An orchestration backend's `orch_collect` returns 0/1 and names mixed results `partial` on `_ORCH_COLLECT_OUTCOME` (it was rc 2).
461	- Usage errors and the startup preflight refusal return 1 (they were 2), and so do the helpers under them: the contract validator in `enforce` mode (`status: preflight_failed` says why), the strategies' work-unit validation, and stage scratch for an unnameable stage. `disposition_halts` answers an off-list word with *halts* (it fails closed; it was a third rc, 2) and `disposition_retryable` with *not retryable*.
462	
463	Verification: `tests/unit/v1-retired-test.sh` R1–R7 and `tests/unit/dispatched-stage-plugins-v2-test.sh` G1/G2 (the contract); `tests/integration/leaf-verdict-halts-test.sh` SPEC-5 (a leaf that writes nothing ends the run); `tests/unit/dispatch-rc-guard-test.sh` SPEC-1/SPEC-16 (every guarded engine file at zero — returns and reads); `tests/unit/core-pipeline-cycle-orchestrator-run-test.sh` and `tests/unit/runner-cycle-rc-action-mapping-test.sh` (outcome words and what the runner does with each, `cycle_abort` distinct from `config_invalid`); `tests/unit/abort-propagation-test.sh` (the abort word); `tests/unit/map-strategy-test.sh` (strategy outcomes); `tests/integration/core-orch-contract-test.sh`, `plugins/tool/orch-sequential/tests/orch-sequential-test.sh`, `plugins/tool/orch-mock/tests/orch-mock-test.sh` (`partial`); `tests/unit/contract-validator-enforce-mode-test.sh`, `tests/integration/preflight-contract-templates-test.sh`, `tests/unit/stage-scratch-test.sh` SPEC-1, `tests/unit/core-pipeline-disposition-test.sh` (the helpers).

70	**(superseded 2026-10-08 by ADR-054 §4 / #1850 — now `orch_collect` returns 0 (all passed) or 1, naming mixed results on `_ORCH_COLLECT_OUTCOME=partial`)**
71	
72	**`orch_collect` exit code convention (all implementations must honour this):**
73	- `0` — all dispatched work units exited 0 (success); pool dir removed.
74	- `1` — all dispatched work units exited non-zero (complete failure).
75	- `2` — mixed results: at least one unit passed and at least one failed (partial). **(superseded 2026-10-08 by ADR-054 §4 / #1850 — now rc 1 + `_ORCH_COLLECT_OUTCOME=partial`)**
76	
77	Work-unit exit codes are normalised — individual codes are not passed through. Strategies use `2` to emit `stage.fail reason=partial` via the runner. **(superseded 2026-10-08 by ADR-054 §4 / #1850 — now rc 1 + `_ZB_STRATEGY_OUTCOME=partial`)**
78	
79	**Phase 0.5 default implementation**: `plugins/tool/orch-sequential/` — single-process, in-order dispatch. Chosen as the default for Phase 0.5 because it has zero coordination surface and the smallest reference impl of the 0/1/2 normalisation contract. The `.zbuild/config.yaml` snippet below shows how to opt in to one of the optional backends.
80	
81	**Parallel implementation**: `plugins/tool/orch-bash-parallel/` — uses bash subshells + `wait -n` for parallelism, no coordination beyond independent execution. Implements `fanout` and `sequential` strategies trivially; `composite` works via a single subshell.
82	
83	**Optional implementation**: `plugins/tool/orch-ruflo-hive/` — proxies to `ruflo hive-mind init/spawn/orchestrate`. Implements all three strategies natively; provides queen-collapse synthesis and shared-memory namespacing. `orch_capabilities` declares `["hive_mind", "queen_collapse", "shared_memory"]`.
84	
85	### Cache backend contract (covered in ADR-010)
86	
87	```bash
88	cache_pull <key> <dest_dir>                           # restore from cache key into dest_dir
89	cache_push <key> <src_dir>                            # snapshot src_dir under cache key
90	cache_capabilities                                    # → JSON
91	```
92	
93	The `<key>` is an opaque, plugin-agnostic identifier (e.g., a slot id or a content hash). The `<dest_dir>` / `<src_dir>` makes the caller's intent explicit and lets a single cache backend serve multiple consumers (resume snapshot, build artifact, etc.) within one run.
94	
95	Reconciled with the code (`core/cache/contract.sh`) on 2026-05-26 per #310: the initial sketch used a single-arg `cache_pull <slot_id>` that conflated key and destination. The two-arg form is what every implementation already needs and what the existing `gh-actions-cache` / `cache-local` plugins ship.
96	
97	Defaults: `local` — a real filesystem-backed cache under `$ZBUILD_CACHE_DIR` (defaults to `~/.zbuild/cache`). Optionals: `gh-actions-cache`, `s3`, `gist`.
98	
99	### Backend selection: `.zbuild/config.yaml`

1	#!/usr/bin/env bash
2	# scripts/lib/stage-limits.sh — the limits a stage's model calls run under.
3	#
4	# One copy, two readers: the router enforces these numbers on every call
5	# (core/router/route.sh) and the engine states them to the stage in its rules
6	# (scripts/lib/stage-prompt.sh, ADR-067 §8). A stage told a different budget
7	# from the one it is killed at works until it is killed.
8	#
9	# Sourced library: inherits the caller's shell options; do NOT add set -euo.
10	[[ -n "${_ZBUILD_STAGE_LIMITS_LOADED:-}" ]] && return 0
11	_ZBUILD_STAGE_LIMITS_LOADED=1
12	
13	if ! declare -F manifest_router_knob >/dev/null 2>&1; then
14	    # shellcheck source=../../core/plugin-registry/manifest-router-budget.sh
15	    source "$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")/../.." && pwd)/core/plugin-registry/manifest-router-budget.sh" 2>/dev/null || true
16	fi
17	
18	# ─── _route_manifest_knob <knob> — ADR-017 §11 (#1816) manifest layer ───────
19	# The dispatched plugin's OWN declared default, read from its manifest via the
20	# dispatch identity the engine exports at plugin_hook_call (ZBUILD_PLUGIN_DIR,
21	# ADR-054 §3 / #1862). Empty whenever there is no dispatch, no manifest, no
22	# declaration — or a declaration this router cannot use.
23	#
24	# Out-of-range and non-numeric values are IGNORED here, not fatal: the loud
25	# gate is validate_manifest at load, and a plugin that got past it with a bad
26	# value must fall back to the constant rather than hand the router a 0-second
27	# timeout. Fail-safe on the hot path, fail-loud at the boundary.
28	_route_manifest_knob() {
29	    local knob="$1"
30	    local dir="${ZBUILD_PLUGIN_DIR:-}"
31	    [[ -n "$dir" && -f "$dir/manifest.yaml" ]] || return 0
32	    declare -F manifest_router_knob >/dev/null 2>&1 || return 0
33	    local v; v="$(manifest_router_knob "$dir/manifest.yaml" "$knob" 2>/dev/null || true)"
34	    [[ "$v" =~ ^[0-9]+$ ]] || return 0
35	    local range; range="$(_manifest_router_range "$knob" 2>/dev/null || true)"
36	    [[ -n "$range" ]] || return 0
37	    local min="${range% *}" max="${range#* }"
38	    [[ "$v" -ge "$min" && "$v" -le "$max" ]] || return 0
39	    printf '%s' "$v"
40	}
41	
42	# ─── _route_resolve_knob — ADR-017 (#455) precedence chokepoint ──────────────
43	# Generic helper: future knobs (tier_default, budget_usd, model_override) reuse
44	# this. Accessor returns per-stage value or empty; env_var supplies session-wide
45	# fallback; manifest_knob (#1816) names the plugin's own declared default; the
46	# compile-time constant is the floor:
47	#
48	#   template accessor  >  env var  >  manifest config.router.*  >  constant
49	#
50	# The manifest sits BELOW env and template because it is a default, not an
51	# override: a flow may right-size a stage for a fast lane, and the operator
52	# escape hatch must still beat both. It sits ABOVE the constant because that is
53	# what the constant always was — a default nobody could state per stage.
54	_route_resolve_knob() {
55	    local accessor_fn="$1" env_var="$2" default_val="$3"
56	    local override_event="${4:-router.timeout.override_ignored}"
57	    local manifest_knob="${5:-}"
58	    local v=""
59	    if [[ -n "${ZBUILD_CURRENT_STAGE:-}" ]] && declare -F "$accessor_fn" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
60	        v="$($accessor_fn "$ZBUILD_CURRENT_STAGE" 2>/dev/null || true)"
61	    fi
62	    if [[ -n "$v" ]]; then
63	        # If env var ALSO set and differs, emit override-ignored event for audit.
64	        # A manifest value losing to template or env is NOT this case: a default
65	        # being replaced is the design, and eventing it would make every
66	        # declaring plugin noisy on every dispatch.
67	        local env_val="${!env_var:-}"
68	        if [[ -n "$env_val" && "$env_val" != "$v" ]]; then
69	            eb_emit_event "$override_event" \
70	                "stage=${ZBUILD_CURRENT_STAGE:-}" \
71	                "env_var=$env_var" \
72	                "env_value=$env_val" \
73	                "applied=$v" 2>/dev/null || true
74	        fi
75	        printf '%s\n' "$v"; return 0
76	    fi
77	    local env_v="${!env_var:-}"
78	    if [[ -n "$env_v" ]]; then
79	        printf '%s\n' "$env_v"; return 0
80	    fi
81	    if [[ -n "$manifest_knob" ]]; then
82	        local mv; mv="$(_route_manifest_knob "$manifest_knob")"
83	        if [[ -n "$mv" ]]; then
84	            printf '%s\n' "$mv"; return 0
85	        fi
86	    fi
87	    printf '%s\n' "$default_val"
88	}
89	
90	# Concrete: per-stage router.timeout_s > $ZBUILD_ROUTER_TIMEOUT >
91	# manifest config.router.timeout_s > 300s default.
92	_route_resolve_timeout() {
93	    _route_resolve_knob template_stage_router_timeout ZBUILD_ROUTER_TIMEOUT 300 \
94	        router.timeout.override_ignored timeout_s
95	}
96	
97	# ADR-018 (#466): per-stage router.max_turns > $ZBUILD_ROUTER_MAX_TURNS > 25 default.
98	# ADR-029 G3 (#812): when the cycle orchestrator detects a router timeout for
99	# this stage, it sets ZBUILD_ROUTER_MAX_TURNS_OVERRIDE so the next dispatch
100	# of the same stage uses an escalated budget (+50%, capped at 2× base). The
101	# override wins over the per-stage template AND the env knob because that's
102	# the entire point — escalation must beat the static config that already
103	# proved too small.
104	_route_resolve_max_turns() {
105	    if [[ "${ZBUILD_ROUTER_MAX_TURNS_OVERRIDE:-}" =~ ^[0-9]+$ ]]; then
106	        printf '%s' "$ZBUILD_ROUTER_MAX_TURNS_OVERRIDE"
107	        return 0
108	    fi
109	    _route_resolve_knob template_stage_router_max_turns ZBUILD_ROUTER_MAX_TURNS 25 \
110	        router.max_turns.override_ignored max_turns
111	}
112	
113	# ADR-018 Amendment N (#762): when max_turns resolves to the 0 sentinel,
114	# classify which source set it (template > env > manifest > default) for
115	# telemetry. Emits `template`, `env`, `manifest` (#1816), or `default`. The
116	# `default` branch is currently unreachable (compile-time default is 25, not 0)
117	# but kept for forward compatibility if the default ever changes.
118	# Copilot review #764: compare numerically so "00", "000" etc. (accepted
119	# by the ^[0-9]+$ validator) classify correctly.
120	_route_classify_max_turns_source() {
121	    local _tpl_val=""
122	    if [[ -n "${ZBUILD_CURRENT_STAGE:-}" ]] \
123	        && command -v template_stage_router_max_turns >/dev/null 2>&1; then
124	        _tpl_val="$(template_stage_router_max_turns "$ZBUILD_CURRENT_STAGE" 2>/dev/null || true)"
125	    fi
126	    local _mf_val; _mf_val="$(_route_manifest_knob max_turns)"
127	    if [[ "$_tpl_val" =~ ^[0-9]+$ ]] && [[ "$_tpl_val" -eq 0 ]]; then
128	        printf '%s' "template"
129	    elif [[ "${ZBUILD_ROUTER_MAX_TURNS:-}" =~ ^[0-9]+$ ]] && [[ "${ZBUILD_ROUTER_MAX_TURNS}" -eq 0 ]]; then
130	        printf '%s' "env"
131	    elif [[ "$_mf_val" =~ ^[0-9]+$ ]] && [[ "$_mf_val" -eq 0 ]]; then
132	        # #1816: a plugin that declares `max_turns: 0` owns that sentinel. Left
133	        # unclassified it would be recorded as `default`, which is the one thing
134	        # it is not — the record would name a source that declared nothing.
135	        printf '%s' "manifest"
136	    else
137	        printf '%s' "default"
138	    fi
139	}
140	
141	# ADR-018 (#467): per-stage router.max_iterations > $ZBUILD_ROUTER_MAX_ITERATIONS > 10 default.
142	_route_resolve_max_iterations() {
143	    _route_resolve_knob template_stage_router_max_iterations ZBUILD_ROUTER_MAX_ITERATIONS 10 \
144	        router.max_iterations.override_ignored
145	}
146	
147	# ADR-029 (#1230): per-stage router.retries > $ZBUILD_ROUTER_RETRIES > 0 default.
148	# The count of retry-on-timeout (rc=124) attempts BEFORE the verbatim-124
149	# fallback. Default 0 (opt-in). Honored by BOTH leaf paths — single-shot
150	# (_route_call_claude) and agentic-loop (route_to_model_loop) — so every leaf
151	# node respects the knob wherever it sits. Out-of-range values (validator
152	# already bounds template 0..10; env is unbounded) clamp to 0 fail-safe.
153	_route_resolve_retries() {
154	    local v; v="$(_route_resolve_knob template_stage_router_retries ZBUILD_ROUTER_RETRIES 0 \
155	        router.retries.override_ignored retries)"
156	    if [[ "$v" =~ ^[0-9]+$ ]] && [[ "$v" -ge 0 ]] && [[ "$v" -le 10 ]]; then
157	        printf '%s' "$v"
158	    else
159	        printf '0'
160	    fi
161	}
